To probe what lies beyond marginal accessibility, we introduce controlled interaction-dominated stress tests, including heterophilic ego-graphs and synthetic Twins tasks whose structural and feature marginals are matched across classes but whose role--feature couplings differ. These results show that high alignment explains much of easy benchmark performance, while low alignment reveals regimes where success requires preserving structure--feature correspondence beyond standard pooled representations.

papers.title: U.S. Data Center Growth Through 2030: A Critical Review of Grid Adequacy and Transmission Expansion Planning
papers.abstract: The growth of large data centers raises questions about both supply adequacy and the suitability of load representations used in connection studies. This paper critically reviews the U.S. demand, generation, and transmission outlook through 2030 and examines the implications for transmission expansion planning (TEP). Comparison of public forecasts highlights distinctions among annual average demand, peak demand, and grid connection capacity. National generating-capacity totals cannot establish a dependable surplus because resource availability, regional adequacy, transmission constraints, and project timing determine supply capability. Recent grid events and published dynamic studies demonstrate that faults can trigger substantial data-center transfers to backup supply, followed by delayed or coordinated demand recovery. These behaviors require appropriate representation within the conventional planning framework, alongside assessment of the requested maximum grid import. The selected literature reveals limited integration of validated data-center dynamic models into the technical screening and economic comparison of expansion alternatives. The review identifies the need to establish whether fault response and recovery change feasible connection capacity, required reinforcement, or the preferred transmission investment.

papers.title: Benchmarking Multilingual Document Understanding in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) perform strongly on multimodal tasks, Document Understanding (DU) among them, but the benchmarks that measure them mostly cover English documents and narrow problems. How well current VLMs generalize across languages, tasks, styles and layouts therefore remains unclear. We introduce MDU, a multilingual DU benchmark of 23146 examples spanning 13 tasks and five languages: English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish. The tasks isolate complementary capabilities, from surface-level text and Markdown extraction through summarization, classification and named-entity recognition to layout-sensitive passage and layout extraction. We evaluate 45 state-of-the-art open-weight VLMs from 1.7B to 235B parameters, plus one commercial system under the same protocol. The benchmark is far from saturated: the best average is 69.0, only eight of the 45 evaluated systems reach 65, and the two best results come from 27B models rather than from the largest systems we evaluate. Performance is uneven in ways that scale does not fix. The gap between the strongest and weakest language does not close as models grow, and it survives controlling for the domain composition of each language. Capabilities also do not improve together: once we partial out overall model quality, per-task scores are largely uncorrelated, and transcription ability in particular trades off against semantic extraction.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Quantization-Aware Neural Channel Estimation with Low-Precision Inference
papers.abstract: Neural channel estimators can improve radio performance of 5G receivers, but real-time deployment in the radio access network (RAN) imposes strict latency and power budgets. Prior studies of quantized neural channel estimators assess this cost through mean-squared error or analytic operation counts. In this paper, we train a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) channel estimator for the 5G NR physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) with INT8 and FP8 quantization-aware training (QAT), and we evaluate its radio performance together with its latency, power, and energy on an NVIDIA H100 GPU. On TDL-A and TDL-C channels at user equipment (UE) speeds up to 35 m/s, both 8-bit models stay within 0.025 dB of FP32 at 10% block error rate (BLER). At batch size 128, INT8 reduces the latency by 16%, the incremental GPU power by 33%, and the energy per query by 26%, compared with 6%, 26%, and 21% for FP8. INT8 is therefore the preferred format.

papers.title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
papers.abstract:
The multivariate breeder's equation $Δ ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\inftyλ_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$. We show that the literal discrete analog of this result is false: with constant positive definite $P$ the iterates can oscillate or diverge. The result is restored by a single additional hypothesis, a uniform bound on the largest eigenvalue of $P_k$, $λ_n$, such that $λ_n(P_k)\le 2/L$ where $L$ is a local Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$. Under this bound the maximum is uniformly stable; under a stricter version together with $\sum_kλ_1(P_k)=\infty$, the maximum is uniformly asymptotically stable. Given these hypotheses, a level-set estimate of the basin of attraction carries over. Both bounds are sharp, and each remaining hypothesis is shown to be necessary. Biologically, the bound says that genetic variance in every direction must be small relative to the curvature of log mean fitness; outside this regime the mean phenotype can overshoot a fitness peak as hypothesized by Fisher's geometric model. As further application of our results, the same conditions apply to the mean update of Gaussian evolutionary optimization algorithms, in which the covariance of the search population plays the role of $G$.

papers.title: A Sublogarithmic Competitive Algorithm for Online Graph Exploration
papers.abstract: In online graph exploration, an agent must visit every vertex of an unknown weighted graph and return to its start, learning the incident edges at each vertex it visits. On $n$-vertex graphs, the best known competitive ratio has been $O(\log n)$, achieved by several algorithms, among them the hierarchical depth-first search of Megow, Mehlhorn, and Schweitzer. We give an algorithm with competitive ratio ${(2+o(1))}\ln n/\ln\ln n$ for known~$n$. Like hierarchical depth-first search, it groups the edges into geometric weight classes and searches depth-first between components of lighter edges. Unlike it, the agent tours each component along a minimum spanning tree for the original weights, so only crossings between components pay for rounding, and the base $b$ of the weight class can grow with~$n$. The leading constant $2$ is tight for our choice of base. Without knowing $n$, restarts with increasing size guesses give upper bounds with leading constant $4$ for a fixed schedule and $2$ in expectation for a randomly shifted schedule. If the weights lie in a known range $[1,2^k]$ with $k\ge4$, choosing $b=k/\log_2 k$ gives a competitive ratio of $O(k/\log k)$ without knowing $n$.

papers.title: Modular $n$-queens in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: A chess queen in $d$-dimensions can move any distance in the direction of any edge or diagonal of the $d$-dimensional hypercube. (That is, a queen can move from a position $x$ to $x+cv$ for any $c$ and any nonzero $v\in\{-1,0,1\}^d$.) We prove that one can place $n^{d-1}$ non-attacking queens on the $d$-dimensional modular board $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ if and only if all prime factors of $n$ exceed $2^d$. The $d=3$ case of this result is a conjecture of van Rees from 1981. Our proof involves both human ideas and substantial AI assistance.

papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Hypersonic Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interaction Dynamics Using Plasma-Generated Disturbances
papers.abstract: The unsteady dynamics of a transitional 3D shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction (SWBLI) are investigated using pulsed plasma disturbances on a cone-slice-ramp geometry in the Boeing/AFOSR Mach-6 Quiet Tunnel. Nanosecond-duration repetitively pulsed spark discharges introduce disturbances which convect through the interaction, causing transient turbulent breakdown in the reattaching shear layer. The unsteady behavior of the separation bubble is characterized using schlieren imaging, and natural broadband unsteadiness is observed in the form of large-scale shock and separation flapping at frequencies below 1500 Hz ($Sr_L< 0.25$). Disturbance packets are introduced at a range of perturbation frequencies and generally induce shear layer oscillations; however, perturbation frequencies below the natural cutoff frequency ($f\approx 1500$ $\mathrm{Hz}$) yield fluctuations with significantly larger amplitudes than those above this frequency. Phase-averaged schlieren images reveal that the disturbances cause a decrease in shear layer height immediately after inducing turbulent breakdown around the reattachment point, with this displacement beginning downstream and moving upstream. The shear layer's response to this displacement is consistent with that of an under-damped dynamic system with a preferred oscillation frequency; the measured frequency of the oscillatory response to external perturbation ($f = 1464$ Hz) is also the approximate cutoff frequency of the natural broadband unsteadiness. Furthermore, the relationship between perturbation frequency and oscillation amplitude resembles that of a low-pass filter, with a cutoff frequency that is within 5\% of the measured oscillator frequency. These experimental findings support the theory that the cutoff frequency for the SWBLI's frequency-selective amplification is tied to the time scale of the weakly damped global mode.

papers.title: Identification of Rational Inattention-Additive Random Utility Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel class of econometric models, called Rational Inattention-Additive Random Utility Models. It is based on the discrete choice rational inattention model of Matvejka and McKay (2015) with additive unobserved heterogeneity incorporated. We show that some of the systematic components of the primitives of the model are nonparametrically identified even if the distributions of unobserved variables and the prior of decision makers are both unknown to the Econometrician. If additional information about the prior is known to the Econometrician, even stronger identification results become available.

papers.title: Damped wave equation with a dynamic boundary condition: sharp resolvent estimate
papers.abstract: This work investigates the stabilization of a wave equation with a localized damping and dynamic boundary conditions. This model traces back to the classical treatment of torsion and impact problems. Consider a second-order hyperbolic equation posed with a dynamic boundary condition on a smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(\M,g)$ with boundary, in which the damping acts either in the interior or on $\d \M$. Under the assumption that the damping is positive on an open subset of its domain of action, a resolvent estimate is established. A logarithmic decay rate is then deduced for the energy of strong solutions. We provide examples that establish the sharpness of the resolvent estimate.

papers.title: From Nodes to Pixels: Topological and Structural Two-View Graph Imaging
papers.abstract: Graph learning still lacks a broadly reusable input interface comparable to patches in vision or tokens in language. Unlike images or text, graphs are irregular, vary in size and density, and are invariant under many equivalent node labelings, making it difficult to standardize inputs across tasks and architectures. We introduce G2Image, a fixed-budget graph imaging framework that converts each graph into two complementary image-like views. TopoGrid provides a stable topological view by encoding an intrinsic bifiltration as a compact multipersistence surface grid, while GraphGrid provides a higher-bandwidth structural view by aggregating edge densities between groups defined by intrinsic node scores. Both views are permutation-invariant and come with resolution-controlled stability guarantees. Because the resulting representations are fixed-size tensors, they can be processed by lightweight 2D encoders and aligned through a supervised cross-view contrastive objective. Across graph classification and molecular prediction benchmarks, G2Image achieves strong average performance among the compared methods, improves over single-view and standard fusion variants, and extends to attribute-rich molecular graphs without changing the overall architecture. These results suggest that fixed-budget graph images offer a practical and reusable interface for graph representation learning.

papers.title: Don't Match the Noise: Distribution Matching under Unknown Measurement Error with an Audit Sample
papers.abstract: Real-world machine learning systems often operate on imperfect measurements: sensors are noisy, annotations are produced by non-experts, and scientific observations are often indirect. In these settings, classic distribution comparison tools such as maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) can be systematically biased, matching artifacts of the measurement process rather than the underlying mechanisms of interest. We study a practical regime in which noisy observations are abundant, but only a small audited subset contains ground-truth measurements. We propose measurement-error-corrected MMD (MEC-MMD), an audit-based estimator that debiases kernel evaluations without requiring a noise model. MEC-MMD is exactly unbiased for the oracle MMD under simple random auditing, admits an explicit variance decomposition, and is consistent for the population MMD, achieving the standard $O_p(N^{-1/2})$ rate when the audit size scales with the dataset. We demonstrate the utility of distributional matching with MEC-MMD loss for both parameter estimation and unsupervised applications, showing that MEC-MMD consistently outperforms MMD and alternative methods. These results provide a principled foundation for robust distribution comparison, simulation-based inference, and learning in noisy real-world machine learning pipelines.

papers.title: UniPipe: Unified Inference Serving and Fine-Tuning for Deadline-Constrained DNN Surrogate Workflows
papers.abstract: DNN surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate scientific workflows that must process high-rate sensor streams in near real time, exemplified by Ptychographic imaging at next-generation X-ray light sources. Such surrogates deliver 100-1000x higher throughput than iterative solvers, enabling faster steering of experiments. To preserve surrogate accuracy during an experiment, as the input distribution evolves, state-of-the-art deployments freeze the pretrained surrogate or run a separate CUDA context that fine-tunes concurrently with serving. However, multi-context concurrency causes significant contention on the GPU, inflating both the mean and the variance of inference latency, triggering deadline misses in workflows where sensor data has to be processed within a hard per-unit deadline. To address this challenge, we propose UniPipe, a single-context system that unifies inference serving and fine-tuning of a DNN surrogate on a single edge GPU. UniPipe is driven by three key insights: both serving and fine-tuning require a forward pass and can be fused into one; the per-sample latency of modern GPUs is non-linear in batch size; and the workload is repetitive across intervals, enabling offline scheduling. Specifically, UniPipe fuses training and inference data in a single forward pass with a selective backward pass on the training subset, and uses a polynomial-time scheduler that exploits the latency curve to compute the batch composition. We evaluate UniPipe on a real-world Ptychographic reconstruction workflow with sensor rates up to 5000 patterns/sec.; UniPipe lowers reconstruction MSE by up to 30% and inference MSE by up to 50% over a pretrained baseline, and reduces the deadline-miss rate by 13%-22% over a multi-context baseline. UniPipe's unified deployment reduces the latency spread from 106% to 57% of the mean, and increases total throughput compared to multi-context baseline.

papers.title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
papers.abstract: We study how many polarized anti-invariant factors of the intermediate Jacobians of smooth Eckardt hyperplane sections determine a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. In rank three, the equation is determined by its fixed cubic surface and a conic in the dual projective space. The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin--Zhang recovers the surface together with one plane section from each factor. When the surface has no automorphisms, these planes can be compared in a common dual space, and reconstruction reduces to classical conic interpolation. Five factors suffice without parameter data, and four suffice with their ordered parameter configuration; both bounds are sharp. In rank two, we construct two-dimensional families of pairwise nonisomorphic equivariant fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. For a fixed fourfold, we also show that the closure of the anti-invariant factor family in an associated OG10 compactification is an integral projective Lagrangian subvariety.

papers.title: Harmonic structure and parametric prediction of instantaneous power in oscillating foils
papers.abstract: A closed-form model is developed to predict the instantaneous lift, pitching moment, and power of an oscillating-foil energy harvester directly from its kinematic input. Such foils extract renewable power from moving water through sinusoidal heaving and pitching. However, due to their large-amplitude motion and vortex-dominated dynamics, classical unsteady aerodynamics cannot accurately predict the time-dependent force and power generation. To generate the model, 405 two-dimensional simulations are computed which vary heave amplitude, pitch amplitude, and frequency, representing the energy harvesting kinematic parameter space. The lift and pitching moment are decomposed into odd Fourier harmonics, and each Fourier coefficient is regressed on sixteen physics-based polynomial terms derived from the kinematic, power, and energy scalings. The regression is performed in two Ridge steps, one for attribution and one for the deployable predictor. The attribution shows that the first harmonic, which contains the mean power, depends on the motion amplitudes. The higher harmonics respond nonlinearly to the frequency, which determines the number and timing of the vortex shedding. The model recovers the cycle-averaged power with a leave-one-out $R^2$ of $0.98$, and reproduces the instantaneous lift with a median peak error of $9\%$ and a median phase error below $1\%$ of the period. The harmonic order of the response counts the discrete vortex events in each stroke, as confirmed by the wake visualization. The model's analytical expression for time-dependent force and power can be utilized as a fast and accurate alternative to high-fidelity simulations, specifically targeting device design and array optimization of oscillating foils.

papers.title: Development of Sapphire-Based Solid-State Neutron Detectors for Fusion Environments
papers.abstract: Single-crystal diamond is the reference solid-state technology for fast neutron detection in fusion devices. Despite this, its complex manufacturing increases their costs and puts limitations on their geometry. Moreover, the limits in their long-term stability and their behaviour in harsh environments further constraint its applications. Synthetic sapphire (Al2O2) is a promising alternative as a solid state detector material: it is available in large, low-cost wafers and features both a wider bandgap and a higher displacement energy compared to diamond. Despite this, it has so far received little-to-no attention as a neutron detector. This work presents the first steps of a development programme for sapphire-based fast neutron detectors. Eight prototypes with 4.5 x 4.5 mm2 and 9 x 9 mm2 active areas and 625 um thickness were fabricated from commercial wafers with Al-Si electrodes and coupled to different electronic configurations. All prototypes detected 5.47 MeV alpha particles from a 241Am source, confirming the viability of both the fabrication process and the use of sapphire as an active material. The small signals (30-40 mV over a peak-to-peak noise of about 8 mV) and the count rate increasing with bias indicate that sapphires will require higher electric fields than the ones experimented in the work (up to about 2.5 kV). Geant4 simulations were also used to estimate the response of a sapphire detector to 14.06 MeV (DT) neutrons, highlighting the perspectives of the detector as a fusion diagnostic.

papers.title: Beyond Ground States: Learning Many-Body Hamiltonians for p-Bit Invertible Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Probabilistic-bit (p-bit) invertible logic encodes a Boolean relation as an energy whose ground states are its legal assignments, computing in any direction by sampling. Traditional constructions target ground-state membership and a wide minimum energy gap, yet finite-time samplers traverse excited states. We cast Hamiltonian design as inverse statistical mechanics: fit an energy with interactions up to order four whose Gibbs law approaches uniformity on each clamp case's legal states, under a gap floor keeping every legal state below every illegal one. Constrained maximum likelihood with pruning and refitting fits terms from a fixed pool, and every delivered energy is audited exactly on all cases. Each energy is scored by time to a verified solution under restarts with its best of nine tuned samplers. In underdetermined modes, learned multipliers factor in 0.55, 0.44, 0.52 and 0.46 [0.38, 0.56] of the hand-written encodings' updates from 4x4 to 7x7, faster within every family below 7x7 at no resolved work penalty; learned adders solve the reverse mode in 0.71 of the updates at 8 bits and about a quarter at 24 and 32 bits, at 0.55 of the work at 32 bits. At 5x5 under equal pool, budget and floor, a gap-maximizing fit reaches 0.79 [0.73, 0.88] in updates and 1.26 in work against the hand-written encoding, while likelihood fitting takes 0.55 [0.46, 0.58] and 0.58 [0.48, 0.61] of the gap fit's updates and work. Rounding coefficients to the narrowest exact integer words tested, we run both energies at each pair's common word on one FPGA color-sweep SSA core, bit-exact with software: learned multipliers take 0.41 of the hand-written encoding's cycles at 4x4 and 0.057 [0.045, 0.068] at 7x7, at up to 2.4 times its lookup tables. The method requires only a circuit's legal assignments; in determined modes, hand-written encodings take less work, and from 12 bits on the adder fewer updates.

papers.title: schubmult: Symbolic algorithms and input-sensitive bounds for Schubert multiplication
papers.abstract: We present schubmult, a GPL-licensed Python system for exact multiplication of ordinary, double, quantum, and quantum double Schubert polynomials, as well as independent-alphabet triple and quantum triple products. Its central algorithm expands one factor into filtered column paths and couples them to Pieri computations on the other factor. Dynamic programming shares intermediate states, and the algorithm returns every Schubert-basis coefficient as an exact arithmetic circuit. We prove input-sensitive operation bounds for the entire product, not just a selected coefficient: for inputs of minimal rank $n$, the classical algorithms have complexity $2^{O(n\log n)}$ and polynomial complexity in $n$ for fixed Lehmer-code lengths. The quantum algorithms have the same general bound and polynomial complexity when, in addition, the number of nonzero entries in the Lehmer code of $v^{-1}$ is fixed. We describe the implementation and distinguish it from the algorithms analyzed, verify computations against independent routines and exact identities, and report reproducible timings for flag and Grassmannian workloads. Parabolic quantum products are treated separately via the Peterson-Woodward comparison.

papers.title: VIDE 2.0: Robust, Scalable Void Finding for Extremely Large Galaxy Surveys
papers.abstract: Current and future spectroscopic and photometric galaxy surveys will deliver unprecedented numbers of galaxies, with expected counts in the tens of millions. To answer the computational challenges posed by these surveys, in this paper we present VIDE 2.0, a significantly improved and enhanced void finding algorithm and analysis pipeline based on VIDE. Leveraging the parameter-free identification of voids via a Voronoi tessellation and watershed scheme, we implement a robust mechanism for handling survey boundaries and incompleteness without relying on vast numbers of boundary particles. This new method identifies edge galaxies and flags voids contaminated by their presence. The mechanism is fully deterministic, producing bit-for-bit reproducible catalogs from identical inputs. An automatic rule for setting the mask resolution renders the entire pipeline parameter-free. Combined with other performance enhancements to the underlying VIDE engine, we find significant ($>100\times$) speedups and a dramatic reduction in memory usage compared to previous versions: a 12-million-galaxy DESI Y1-class mock catalog now completes in roughly 15 minutes on a single laptop, where VIDE 1.0 could not run a catalog of even $10^6$ galaxies on the same hardware. We are also able to identify voids existing closer to survey boundaries via deterministic per-void contamination flags, maximizing their statistical potential. We exercise the upgraded pipeline on two large mock suites (MultiDark-Patchy DR12 and AbacusSummit DESI Y1 ELG), demonstrating converged cosmic-variance covariances for the void number function, the void-galaxy cross-correlation, and the void ellipticity distribution -- key ingredients for Stage IV void cosmology. VIDE 2.0 is now well suited to handle large numbers of galaxies in mock and real observations, and ready to tackle the challenges of future campaigns.

papers.title: Reconstructing Fine-grained Memory Reuse Structure in GPU Kernels
papers.abstract: Optimizing GPU data movement requires knowing which instructions access the same data and across which execution scopes reuse occurs. Existing profilers can attribute memory behavior to individual instructions but do not expose the reuse relations among them, while aliasing, dynamic indexing, and runtime parameters prevent static analysis from establishing these relations in general. Cycle-level simulation can reconstruct such relations, but at costs prohibitive for production workloads. We introduce two abstractions for representing this structure: Topological Distance, which labels each dynamic memory access with the smallest execution scope (thread, warp, block, or grid) containing its most recent reuse, and PCDepGraph, which organizes these labels into a PC-level graph of the kernel's memory reuse structure. Defined over logical execution scopes rather than transient hardware state, the representation remains stable across runs and GPU targets while directly indicating the sharing scope that candidate optimization mechanisms must cover. Our tool, cuVein, reconstructs PCDepGraph directly from optimized binaries, without sampling, at generally under 10x overhead. Across HPC and AI workloads on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and H100, optimizations guided by PCDepGraph eliminate up to 90.18% of memory instructions and yield up to 2.84x kernel speedup; reuse-scope distributions remain consistent across platforms, supporting that the representation captures program structure rather than transient hardware behavior.

papers.title: General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
papers.abstract: We develop a gauge-independent theory of magnetic reconnection beyond the standard special-relativistic framework of inertial systems in flat spacetime. Our definitions of reconnection and its rate are independent of reference frame and coordinate system, allowing physical effects of gravity and net linear acceleration to be distinguished from coordinate effects. We extend the mesoscale theory of Liu et al. [PRL 118, 085101 (2017)], in which the reconnection rate depends on physics both within the diffusion region and in an upstream ideal, force-free region. The theory identifies three non-inertial and curved-spacetime (NICS) effects, including gravitationally induced magnetic tension: gravitational distortion of the reconnection plane changes the curvature of magnetic field lines. Applying the theory to a simplified accretion plasma near )a compact object, we find that (1) whether gravity increases or decreases the reconnection rate depends on the system's orientation relative to the gravitational source, with the greatest increase occurring when the outflow jet points toward or away from the source; and (2) the magnitude of the gravitational effect scales with the dimensionless parameter $\barκ \equiv r_sΔy^2/r^3$, where $r$ is the Schwarzschild radial coordinate, $r_s$ is the source's Schwarzschild radius, and $Δy$ is the mesoscale length.

papers.title: Fragility of Aeolian Ripples
papers.abstract: Sand surfaces exposed to the wind are covered by aeolian sand waves of diverse wavelengths, from centimetres for small ripples to decameters for dunes. Sand dunes can be said to be antifragile, since their growth is not prohibited by storms, whereas ripples and megaripples are fragile since they get flattened. The fluid-entrainment hypothesis attributes their fragility to a common cause: the spontaneous aerodynamic entrainment of grains. Here, we challenge this conventional view by revealing its major shortcomings and inconsistencies. An alternative framework, routed in the granular bed rheology, posits that impact ripples are erased when the two-phase flow of ballistically hopping grains on a solid sand surface gives way to a three-phase flow, featuring an intermediate, collision-dominated, fluid-like transport layer. Notably, both martian wind-drag ripples and terrestrial aerodynamic ripples, which emerge via a hydrodynamic instability, are insensitive to such "surface-melting". Their destruction is predicated on the transition from aerodynamically smooth to rough conditions, instead. Our theoretical arguments are well supported by a stability diagram in terms of Shields number and grain diameter, assembled from a carefully reassessed large body of literature, and backed up by dedicated control measurements.

papers.title: Exploring 3-CNF Formulas Generated From Partial Steiner Triple Systems
papers.abstract: Steiner triple systems (STS) and subsets of these known as partial STS (PSTS) are combinatorial objects that have received substantial interest from mathematicians since their introduction in 1847. Over the last three decades, (P)STS have found applications in diverse fields ranging from digital circuit testing to wireless transmission. Perhaps unsurprisingly, the triple in (P)STS allows for a mapping to 3-conjunctive normal form (3-CNF) formulas, the Boolean formula used as input to 3-SAT. Prompted by this ready conversion of (P)STS to 3-CNF formulas and numerous real-world applications of (P)STS, we explore the intersection of (P)STS with 3-SAT and its counting version \#3-SAT. We explain the properties of (P)STS-generated 3-CNF formulas in terms familiar to the SAT community and experimentally compare them against randomly-generated 3-CNF formulas. We find that PSTS-3-CNF formulas are statistically distinct from randomly generated 3-CNF formulas, in both probability of satisfiability and expected solution count.

papers.title: Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
papers.abstract: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

papers.title: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
papers.abstract: Observational causal discovery often leaves causal di- rections unresolved or unstable. Large language mod- els (LLMs) can provide semantic information to resolve these directions, but incorrect proposals can exclude the true causal graph and invalidate downstream inference. We study three separate decisions: where to allocate semantic queries, which proposals to admit, and which causal graphs to retain. Our framework distinguishes population non-identifiability from finite-sample insta- bility, evaluates semantic orientation against statistical and random controls, and examines calibrated admis- sion and error-tolerant DAG retention. Experiments across benchmark networks show that semantic infor- mation improves recovery over coin-flip orientations, but targeting unstable edges has no established ad- vantage over matched-random allocation. The tested admission certificate cannot support nontrivial admis- sion with the available calibration tasks. Moreover, downstream retention depends on reference adequacy: learned references contain the true DAG in only three of 80 planned tasks. These findings separate the value of semantic information from the reliability of its alloca- tion, admission, and retention, and identify calibration size and reference adequacy as key limitations.

papers.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 5: cyclic total variation
papers.abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses \emph{exactly} to \(β_c(n)=β_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(γ_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the \emph{linear} statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\sqrt{K_0N}\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/β_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.

papers.title: La Silla-QUEST RR Lyrae Survey III: The Shape of the Outer Virgo Overdensity
papers.abstract: Using the La Silla-QUEST and Gaia surveys, we identify 256 RR Lyrae stars (RRLS) in the Outer Virgo Overdensity (OVOD). These show that the OVOD has a signifcantly larger and more complex shape than previously recognized. The OVOD lies at an average distance of $\sim 85$ kpc, has a long dimension of $\sim 57^\circ$ ($\sim 85$ kpc), and a width that varies from $\sim 10^\circ $ ($\sim 15$ kpc) to $\sim 35^\circ $ ($\sim 50$ kpc) in a prominent bulge. Because it bends by $\sim 35^\circ$ from a great circle, it does not appear to be a stellar stream. The type ab RRLS (RRab) span a large range in period, with a mean of $0.59$ days, and only $19\pm 3 \%$ lie near the locus of Oosterhoff II variables in the Bailey diagram. The overall large number of RRLS along with a mean RRab metallicity ([Fe/H]) of -1.60 and $1 σ$ dispersion of 0.32, as inferred from the RRab periods, suggest that the OVOD progenitor was a large dwarf galaxy. The hypothesis that the OVOD may be a shell produced by the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger \citep{chandra2023} is supported by the $\sim 70^\circ$ angle that the southern extension of the OVOD makes with the orbits of red giants in its central part. The complex shape of the overall RRLS distribution, including a small north-south distance gradient, may also indicate, however, that we are seeing a blended, composite structure projected on the sky.

papers.title: Origins of Satellite-System Building Blocks I: Solid Delivery During Jupiter's Growth
papers.abstract: Jupiter's satellites formed within a circumplanetary disk (CPD), but the origin and delivery of the solids from which they accreted remain uncertain. Here, we investigate the delivery of planetesimal material to the CPD while consistently accounting for the growth of Jupiter and the evolution of its surrounding planetesimal reservoir. Using N-body simulations coupled to an evolving CPD model, we quantify the solid mass supplied through planetesimal ablation and direct capture. We find that, although proto-Jupiter rapidly opens a gap in the planetesimal disk, planetesimals continue to enter the CPD for more than 1 Myr. Under efficient ablation, the mass deposited in the CPD can reach approximately 1 Me, about one order of magnitude higher than the mass delivered through direct capture. However, the low efficiency of pebble accretion within the CPD implies that forming the Galilean satellites from ablated material alone may require a very large pebble reservoir. Directly captured planetesimals, despite contributing less total mass, can instead provide satellitesimals that grow through mutual collisions and serve as seeds for subsequent pebble accretion. Our results therefore favor a hybrid formation pathway in which the Galilean satellites grow through a combination of satellitesimal and pebble accretion. We further demonstrate that even a planetesimal reservoir containing less solid material than the minimum-mass solar nebula can supply sufficient building blocks to form the Galilean satellites. The balance between the ablation and direct capture depends sensitively on the efficiency of aerodynamic heating: if ablation is weaker than commonly assumed, direct capture can become the dominant source of satellite building blocks. These results connect the formation of Jupiter and its satellites by showing how Jupiter's growth regulates both the duration and form of solid delivery to its CPD.

papers.title: Characterization of the mechanical vibrations of the Schmidt Camera at the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory
papers.abstract: Mechanical vibrations in astronomical telescopes can degrade image quality, making their detection and characterization essential. This work presents the development and validation of a low-cost, portable vibration monitoring system based on MEMS accelerometers interfaced with a microcontroller. The system integrates sensor acquisition and data analysis capabilities and was evaluated through controlled laboratory tests. The system was subsequently deployed at the historic Schmidt Camera of the Tonantzintla Astronomical Observatory in Mexico. After more than 80 years of operation, this study represents the first characterization of its mechanical vibrations. Preliminary measurements reveal dominant frequency components and their corresponding amplitudes, providing insight into the telescope's dynamic behavior and potential structural couplings that may affect image quality. Understanding the vibrational environment of astronomical telescopes is essential for the successful integration of new instrumentation. Identifying vibration frequencies and amplitudes can support the development of mitigation strategies, data filtering techniques, and numerical simulations to predict image quality degradation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of low-cost inertial sensing for monitoring heritage-class telescopes and provide a foundation for future instrumentation and preservation efforts at the Tonantzintla Observatory.

papers.title: A New Framework for Quantum Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Quantum reinforcement learning (QRL) has emerged as a promising approach for controlling quantum systems and accelerating learning tasks with quantum resources. However, most existing QRL formulations still retain a classical reinforcement learning interface: states and actions are often encoded in computational bases and rewards are extracted through measurements. This interface is restrictive for genuinely quantum environments: choosing a measurement can discard entanglement information, while repeated intermediate measurements collapse the evolving state and require costly re-preparation. This motivates a fully QRL framework in which the agent, environment, rewards, and return accumulation are all quantum. In this paper, we take a step toward this goal and introduce a new QRL framework in which both the policy and the environment are modeled by conditional quantum channels. We then propose a quantum policy-gradient algorithm for parameterized conditional quantum channels with a trainable control basis. We also derive finite- and infinite-horizon gradient estimators using a new parameter-shift rule. This rule is needed because policy parameters are shared across repeated interaction blocks and the infinite-horizon objective is not a finite circuit; rather than shifting every occurrence and evaluating the whole trajectory, our estimator shifts only one sampled policy block. Sampling this block from a geometric distribution yields an unbiased gradient estimator under bounded rewards. Finally, we establish convergence of the resulting stochastic gradient-ascent procedure to stationary points under standard smoothness and step-size assumptions.

papers.title: Connected regular $Γ$-distance magic graphs with magic constant zero
papers.abstract: Let $(Γ,+)$ be a finite Abelian group. A $Γ$-distance magic labeling of a graph is a bijection from its vertex set to $Γ$ such that the sum of the labels of the neighbours of each vertex is a fixed element of $Γ$, called the magic constant. The constructions of Kovář and collaborators provide regular distance magic graphs of odd order with consecutive integer labels for every even degree from $4$ to $14$. We adapt these constructions to prove the existence of connected $r$-regular $(A\times\mathbb{Z}_n)$-distance magic graphs with magic constant $0$, where $A$ is any finite Abelian group of odd order, $n$ is odd, and $r\in\{4,6,8,10,12,14\}$, under explicit sufficient conditions on $n$. Here $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. It suffices to take $n\ge13$ for $r=6$, $n\ge19$ for $r=14$, and $n\ge15$ for $r\in\{4,8,10,12\}$.

papers.title: SunLightBots: Turning sunlight into self-sustained, high-power motion in soft robots
papers.abstract: Soft robots built from active materials can directly convert environmental stimuli into motion, offering a route to energy autonomy and embodied control. However, environmental energy is generally harvested at low power, whereas rapid, mechanically demanding actions require high mechanical output power. Reconciling this mismatch while sustaining self-regulated cyclic actuation is challenging, particularly at the subgram scale, where limited payload capacity constrains the integration of conventional power and control hardware. Here, we present SunLightBots, a class of subgram, sunlight-powered, untethered soft robots that achieve autonomous locomotion under continuous illumination near 1 Sun (100 mW/cm2). Their operation is enabled by a self-resetting snapping (SRS) mechanism that integrates liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) with snap-through instability to accumulate solar energy supplied at low power, release it as rapid, high-power motion, and reset through photothermal-mechanical feedback. Through coordinated optimization of the LCE actuation temperature, photothermal conversion, actuation stress, and structural energy barrier, the system operates near 1 Sun and achieves a peak mass-specific mechanical power of 89 W/kg. At this irradiance, the optimized LCE generates an actuation stress of 0.1 MPa at approximately 60 deg C. SunLightBots demonstrate sustained swimming, crawling, and repeated impulsive jumping. Under 1.5 Suns, the swimmer advances more than three body lengths per cycle. This work provides a materials-mechanics route toward autonomous soft robots powered entirely by the environment.

papers.title: SyntheIce: A Synthetic Radargram Annotation Benchmark for Englacial Layer Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Englacial layers in radio-echo-sounding radargrams (subsurface ice images) encode the climate and flow history of ice sheets and glaciers. However, large-scale extraction is hindered by time-consuming manual annotation and semi-automated detectors that produce fragmented rather than continuous horizons. We address two challenges: reconstructing complete layers from partial detections across radargram profiles and validating layer continuity across adjacent tile boundaries. We introduce a slope-aware greedy fragment-linking algorithm that reconstructs full-width layers using row-similarity gating and an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) slope predictor. Each reconstruction receives a content-based hash ID for stable cross-radargram identification. For quantitative evaluation, we generate SyntheIce, a synthetic dataset of 600 radargrams spanning multiple complexity levels and realistic noise conditions, including 150 wide radargrams divided into four adjacent tiles. All samples include exact ground-truth annotations. We evaluate the dataset using XCheck, a consistency-based validation framework, extending its original two-image setting to four consecutive tiles and enforcing continuity at every boundary. This demonstrates the dataset's utility for developing and evaluating real-world annotation algorithms. Our findings extend beyond ice science: when spatial features are fragmented but retain consistent local geometry, trajectory-based linking is more reliable than appearance-based matching. Evaluation against expert-labeled real radargrams demonstrates high precision, recall, F1-score, and mean IoU, supporting the method's transfer to real-world data.

papers.title: Susceptibility Bottlenecks in Equilibrium Propagation Using Oscillator Ising Machines
papers.abstract: Equilibrium propagation (EP) enables learning in physical systems by exploiting the displacement between free and weakly perturbed equilibrium states. Here, we investigate how the underlying oscillator dynamics govern the transmission of learning signals in oscillator Ising machines (OIMs). We show that the hidden-layer response can be decomposed into two distinct factors: the nudging force applied at the output and the susceptibility governing its transmission to the hidden layer. Using a bipartite OIM with interactions interpolating between phase-difference and phase-sum coupling, we investigate these factors while ensuring that all coupling forms realize the same Ising Hamiltonian at binary phase-locked states. We demonstrate that second-harmonic injection primarily influences the nudging force through phase binarization, whereas the coupling form controls the cross-layer susceptibility through the mixed curvature of the energy landscape. At equal mixing, the mixed curvature vanishes on the binary manifold, strongly suppressing hidden-layer learning signals. Numerical simulations validate these mechanisms and reveal their consequences for classification performance. Our findings establish that realizing a desired energy landscape alone is insufficient to ensure effective physical learning; the system must also support the transmission of perturbations required for learning.

papers.title: Comparison of the flamelet progress variable and thickened flame models for LES of turbulent combustion
papers.abstract: Large-eddy simulation (LES) of turbulent combustion requires closure models for unresolved flame structures and chemical processes. Two widely used but fundamentally different approaches are the flamelet/progress-variable approach (FPVA) and the dynamically thickened-flame model (TFM). Here, both are applied to methane-air combustion within a common numerical framework and evaluated for the Sandia D flame and a jet-in-crossflow representative of a non-assist waste-gas flare across a range of crosswind-to-jet velocity ratios. For the predominantly diffusion-controlled Sandia-D flame, FPVA and TFM exhibit similar accuracy, while FPVA is substantially less computationally expensive and converges faster under mesh refinement. More detailed chemical kinetics improve agreement with experimental measurements, with little additional cost for FPVA but a substantial increase for TFM. For the jet-in-crossflow, both approaches reproduce the experimentally observed reduction in combustion efficiency with increasing crosswind, but their predictions progressively diverge as the crosswind strength increases. This divergence coincides with the emergence of a locally premixed reaction branch captured by TFM but not represented by FPVA, whereas predictions in diffusion-dominated regions remain broadly similar. In TFM, the locally premixed branch is associated with elevated scalar dissipation and greater residual methane downstream, indicating that highly strained premixed combustion contributes to differences in predicted flare performance. These results show that FPVA and TFM can provide similar predictions in diffusion-dominated flames but differ substantially when crossflow induces locally premixed, highly strained combustion near the nozzle.

papers.title: On open weakly 2-semiconvex sets with nonempty 2-nonsemiconvexity-point sets in three-dimensional Euclidean space
papers.abstract: We study general topological properties of open weakly $2$-semiconvex sets in real three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$. An open set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is called weakly $2$-semiconvex if through every boundary point of the set there passes a closed half-plane that does not intersect the set. The largest subset of the complement of a given set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every closed half-plane intersecting this subset also intersects the given set is called the $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set corresponding to the given one. We prove that the nonempty $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set corresponding to an open weakly $2$-semiconvex set is open and weakly $2$-semiconvex. We also construct a weakly $2$-semiconvex domain whose $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set is an unbounded domain that can be either convex or nonconvex.

papers.title: Harmony: Bridging Audio Understanding and Editing through Agentic Collaboration
papers.abstract: Natural-language audio editing requires connecting a user's intent to specific sounds and time regions while preserving surrounding content. Complex requests make this connection demanding: an edit may select one occurrence, depend on a temporal relation, or modify a source that overlaps with other sounds. We introduce Harmony, an agentic framework that bridges audio understanding and editing through collaboration among an LLM planner, an audio-language model, and external tools. Harmony combines two mechanisms. Edit-driven collaborative planning uses targeted questions and tool measurements to determine the target, timing, and operation parameters. Evidence-guided execution uses observations of the first separated or generated audio to trigger bounded corrections before final mixing. Together, these mechanisms connect semantic decisions to waveform operations throughout the editing process. Harmony supports addition, removal, replacement, and volume adjustment. On 420 MMAE examples spanning these operations, Harmony achieves an exact match rate of 22.62%, compared with 13.57% for the strongest baseline, and improves aggregate instruction following and context preservation.

papers.title: The Gaia-alerted 2024--2025 brightening of V346 Nor
papers.abstract: Young stellar objects (YSOs) build their final mass through a highly unsteady, episodic accretion process, often accompanied by outflow and ejection events. Objects undergoing episodic high-accretion states are known as eruptive YSOs. V346 Nor is an embedded eruptive YSO that underwent a sudden optical brightening in 2024 July that triggered an alert from the Gaia Photometric Science Alert system. With the aim of characterizing the physical processes behind this recent brightening event, we analyze new and archival photometric and spectroscopic monitoring data. We study how the brightness, colors, and spectral features changed with time in the past decade. We also fitted an accretion disk model to the observations in which the stellar mass--accretion rate product $M_{\star}\dot{M}$ and the line-of-sight extinction $A_V$ are free parameters. The accretion rate in V346 Nor has been higher ($M_{\star}\dot{M} \sim 10^{-4}\,M_{\odot}^2\,$yr$^{-1}$) since 2021 than during any previous historical peak, although it was relatively constant during the 2025 February-May brightness maximum, which was driven instead by a drop in extinction from $A_V \approx 20$\,mag to $10$\,mag. V346 Nor has accreted about 2\% of the stellar mass since its outburst. A P Cygni profile in H$α$ indicates a strong outflowing wind reminiscent of classical FUors. The variability of the CaII infrared triplet lines and transient CO bandhead emission point to a highly unstable inner disk and accretion region. The persistence of forbidden line emission indicates ongoing jet activity. The brightness and color variations of V346 Nor are the result of a superposition of changes in the accretion rate and the line-of-sight extinction. With record-high accretion levels and strong wind and jet activity, V346 Nor is in one of its most active phases since its original outburst in the 1970s.

papers.title: Fatigue crack growth without plasticity under cyclically reversed shear
papers.abstract: We show that cyclic fatigue can occur in a system whose elements behave elastically up to an irreversible failure threshold, without plasticity, friction, or any time-dependent process. The model represents a weak interface between two elastic bodies loaded in shear. Under sufficiently large cyclic loading below the static failure threshold, a pre-existing flaw advances progressively, by a few lattice spacings per cycle. Two conditions are needed for this behavior: each bond fails more easily under one sense of the shear than the opposite, and the shear must be reversed during the cycle by an amount large enough to break bonds that have not yet failed. The model thus identifies the minimal conditions for an intrinsic, plasticity-free fatigue mechanism. Such conditions may be met at interfaces and weak planes subjected to strongly reversed shear, as in fretting, rolling contact, and reversed torsion, or in cyclic shear of cemented granular materials.

papers.title: Time Advances and Dispersive Constraints in Dressed Gravitational Scattering
papers.abstract: We derive a low energy group time advance in 4D dressed gravitational scattering at leading eikonal order with full soft dependence for a sharp dressing profile of finite soft scale. Dispersive matching of nonnegative absorption excludes the amplitude's analytic crossing with high energy boundedness. This reflects internal scales growing with energy via string diffusion in quantum gravity and high energy nonlinear graviton rescattering, coupled to soft clouds beyond leading soft order. Interference preserving joint detection of hard particles and coherent soft radiation may reveal the advance.

papers.title: Force-Dependent Change of Structural Behavior Upon Pulling a Grafted Flexible Polymer
papers.abstract: Manipulating polymer chains by means of experimental instruments such as optical tweezers has helped understand better the effects of molecular forces in macromolecular structures. In this study, we simulate the influence of a pulling force on structural phases of a coarse-grained model for flexible polymers using generalized-ensemble Monte Carlo methodologies. The recently introduced microcanonical inflection-point analysis method is employed to identify and classify structural phases of the system. Specific order parameters help characterize the transition behavior in response to the present pulling force. We show that, upon increasing the pulling strength, the coil-globule transition turns from second to first order, then merges with the liquid-solid transition. An intermediate phase, separating the coil and globule phases, is identified for certain force strengths. Clear evidence of the Gough-Joule effect is found as well. Transitions do not occur at all if the pulling force exceeds a certain threshold value.

papers.title: Martingale posteriors for flexible regression via recursive least squares
papers.abstract: Predictive Bayes quantifies uncertainty by specifying a sequence of one-step-ahead predictive distributions, inducing a martingale posterior without an explicit prior. Existing parametric constructions rely on stochastic-gradient updates and have seen limited development for flexible regression. We propose a predictive Bayes framework based on recursive least squares, whose martingale posterior has an explicit representation: given future covariates, it is the law of the posterior mean plus a weighted series of independent draws from the standardized predictive distribution. The posterior mean is a penalized least squares estimator, available in closed form and invariant to data ordering, whereas the predictive distribution, for example heavy tailed, is chosen separately without changing the estimator or algorithm. We derive the exact posterior variance under a known design and an asymptotically Gaussian approximation, and obtain the martingale posterior in closed form for Gaussian predictive distributions. Posterior draws are independent by construction, with a known truncation error, and require no Markov chain Monte Carlo. The construction extends to additive, mixed and Gaussian process models. In simulations and an analysis of NHANES triglyceride data, the method attains accuracy comparable to that of a fully Bayesian model with the same response distribution at a fraction of its computational cost.

papers.title: Stochastic Dominance in Discrete Parking Processes on Graphs
papers.abstract: In a recent study on the one-dimensional discrete parking process, it was conjectured that the number of occupied sites in the sequential model first-order stochastically dominates its static counterpart on any path graph. In this paper, we first prove this conjecture for all path graphs and then explore whether stochastic dominance holds for general graph topologies. We show that the property extends naturally to all cycle graphs, and an exhaustive computational analysis confirms that it holds for all 31 connected simple graphs with fewer than 6 vertices. For graphs with 6 or more vertices, we demonstrate that this dominance does not hold universally by constructing explicit counterexamples in which the static model dominates the sequential one; moreover, while one model always dominates the other for all connected graphs with up to 7 vertices, we show that stochastic comparability fails starting at 8 vertices. We also prove that stochastic dominance is inherited by disjoint unions when all connected components share the same dominance direction, and we exhibit mixed unions in which stochastic comparability is either preserved or lost. Finally, supported by algorithmic computations, we formulate a conjecture proposing that the dominance of the sequential model over the static one holds for all graphs with maximum degree at most 3.

papers.title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: Cross-Attribute Externalities of Fairness Interventions
papers.abstract: Fairness interventions often targets disparities associated with a single sensitive attribute in binary classification tasks. However, when multiple sensitive attributes are associated with a data subject, improving fairness with respect to one attribute does not necessarily improve it across all attributes: it may exacerbate disparities associated with other sensitive attributes, including those that are unavailable to the practitioner. We refer to these unintended effects as cross-attribute externalities of fairness. We study how fairness with respect to one sensitive attribute varies when an initially unfair classification or regression model is corrected with respect to another attribute. We characterize these externalities using Wasserstein barycentric disparities and develop a distributional framework that captures changes in both marginal and joint fairness measures. This highlights a limitation of conventional fairness evaluation, in which the success of an intervention is assessed mainly for the attribute it targets. In a jointly Gaussian model, we derive explicit trajectories for marginal and joint disparities and identify conditions under which an intervention eliminates disparities with respect to its target attribute while increasing disparities associated with another attribute. We also derive sharp partial-identification bounds on the resulting externalities when a sensitive attribute is unavailable and extend our results to categorical sensitive attributes. We illustrate these externalities using classification and regression real-data: in the classification experiments, interventions increase unfairness with respect to the hidden attribute in the majority of scenarios across more than half of the datasets considered; in the regression experiments on the ACSIncome dataset, correcting for race reduces sex disparities, whereas subsequently correcting for age increases them.

papers.title: A Three-Stage Unsupervised Online Physics-Informed Neural Network for Microgrid Optimal Power Flow
papers.abstract: Optimal allocation of generators is a key challenge in power systems to achieve economical dispatch while satisfying operational constraints. Conventional optimization techniques can be computationally expensive, limiting their applicability in real-time environments, and neural networks often require offline retraining under new operating conditions. This paper proposes a three-stage unsupervised online physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for optimal power flow (OPF). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework satisfies load demand and system constraints while achieving a $43,665 lower operating cost than fmincon-based optimization under the same operating conditions. The training process analysis further demonstrate the framework's ability to adapt its parameters online to variations in load demand and renewable generation in real time.

papers.title: Robust Decoupled Input Filtering for Internal Model Principle-Based Output Regulation of Polynomial Exogenous Signals
papers.abstract: Internal model principle-based controllers regulate polynomial references and disturbances exactly, but only asymptotically, and their transient input can peak and oscillate, increasingly so as the degree of the exogenous signals grows. A filter placed in series with the plant smooths the command but alters the closed-loop spectrum and can destroy stability. We propose an architecture that keeps the filter outside the loop the regulator stabilizes: the internal model is driven by the error of an ideal, unfiltered copy of the plant, the physical plant receives the filtered command, and an auxiliary plant copy absorbs the mismatch between the two inputs. If the filter satisfies blocking conditions at the origin, any gains that stabilize the unfiltered loop can be combined with any such filter without losing regulation of the true error. Under additive plant uncertainty, we derive a small-gain condition that guarantees robust stability and regulation. On a scalar plant, the proposed controller produces a smoother input and a larger input-delay margin than the unfiltered one, and it maintains regulation under a large loss of actuator effectiveness. On a three-mass chain, its tolerance to unmodeled actuator dynamics and delay stays essentially constant as the regulator is made more aggressive.

papers.title: The Closest Super-Eccentric Giant Planet: Dynamical History and Orbital Future of Gaia-3b
papers.abstract: With new high-resolution spectra and radial velocities (RVs) from the NEID spectrometer, we reaffirm the planetary designation of the previously identified super-eccentric giant planet Gaia~3b. Our additional 23 RVs span 356 days, including an RV observation obtained within hours of the periastron passage. By modeling all of the available RVs we collapse a previously tri-modal orbital period posterior distribution and report a more precisely measured value of $P=331.52\pm0.02$ days. Our measure of the eccentricity ($e=0.9462\pm0.0017$) is in agreement with previous measurements and thus corroborates the status of Gaia~3b as the third most eccentric planet known to date. We generate synthetic realizations of the Gaia astrometric time series and derived RUWE to show that only the planetary-companion and close to equal-mass binary cases are plausible when compared to the reported RUWE. We then show that the close to equal-mass binary case is unlikely based on the Gaia color-magnitude position and the shape and amplitude of the bisectors measured from the NEID cross-correlation functions. The confirmation of Gaia~3b's planetary status makes it the closest known super-eccentric giant planet ($d \approx 35$ pc) and leads us to anticipate that Gaia DR4 will detect more super-eccentric planets orbiting nearby Sun-like stars. Finally, due to the presence of a distant stellar companion, we demonstrate that a plausible pathway exists for excitation of the planet's eccentricity by von Zeipel-Kozai-Lidov oscillations.

papers.title: Methodological Pitfalls in Predicting Ship Turnaround Time at Brazilian Ports: An Empirical Audit and a Reproducible Pipeline
papers.abstract: Two recent studies on ship turnaround time at Brazilian ports report models with R-squared scores above 0.80 on data from the national waterway transportation agency. We audit their published datasets and reveal these results are inflated by structural data leakage. Specifically, 97 percent of berthing events in their random row-level split appear in both training and testing partitions. We demonstrate that a model's R-squared drops from 0.82 to 0.20 when the data is properly split at the berthing level. We further document additional methodological flaws, including survivorship bias, undocumented target truncation, and the retention of variables that algebraically reconstruct the target. To address these issues, we propose a reproducible pipeline that aggregates cargo to the berthing level, utilizes conditional imputation, and represents high-cardinality cargo variables through weighted averages of multilingual sentence embeddings. Evaluating six time targets and thirty seeds, our pipeline reveals that cargo embeddings yield statistically significant improvements on four operational targets, while administrative waiting times remain unaffected. Prior works missed this per-target heterogeneity by conflating genuine signal with leaked identity.

papers.title: Joint Beamforming and Duplex-Mode Segment Selection for Secure Uplink Transmission in Pinching Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have recently emerged as a promising architecture for reconfigurable, flexible and proximity-driven signal delivery. In this paper, we propose a segmented waveguide-based PASS architecture for enabling secure uplink communications, where each segment activates at most one pinching antenna (PA), which inherently eliminates the inter-antenna re-radiation effect and yields a tractable uplink signal model. To protect the uplink transmission against eavesdropping, the base station (BS) injects artificial noise (AN) toward the eavesdroppers via selected downlink segments using a duplex-mode segment selection mechanism, which dynamically configures each segment for either uplink reception or downlink AN transmission through switch-controlled fiber connections. We formulate the secrecy energy efficiency (SEE) maximization problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) that jointly optimizes the receive beamforming vector, AN covariance, user transmit power, pinching antenna positions, and duplex-mode segment assignment. Given the non-convex and combinatorial nature of the problem, we develop an efficient alternating optimization (AO) framework, where the resulting subproblems are solved using the Dinkelbach method combined with successive convex approximation (SCA) and penalty-based relaxation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of SEE and robustness against waveguide attenuation. Moreover, AN effectively suppresses information leakage, while PA mobility, duplex-mode segment allocation, and waveguide segmentation further improve secrecy performance through flexible positioning and reduced in-waveguide propagation loss.

papers.title: Symmetry adapted tensor networks and quantum classical geometric learning for hadronic tomography: a proton construction
papers.abstract: We construct a calibrated model of the proton generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distribution (GTMD) $F_{1,1}$ in the real, staple-even valence-$u$ sector at zero skewness. Experimental measurements, lattice matrix elements, and phenomenological distributions enter through a single shared light-front state, organized as a symmetry-resolved tree tensor network in which color-singlet structure, exchange statistics, and the additive $J_z$ and $I_z$ charges are built in. Classical and quantum geometric nodes represent the residual transverse response. The GTMD is defined with soft subtraction, one-loop nonsinglet matching, NLO collinear evolution, and an explicit nonperturbative joint closure, so that each input is used with its own operator convention and scale. Calibrating against correlated ART25 transverse projections, HERA inclusive data, and lattice, elastic, and static information gives a simple picture. The forward inputs narrow the attainable transverse response by about $81\%$ at $x=0.4$. The simultaneous dependence on quark momentum and momentum transfer, however, is untouched by any of them: a deformation that leaves every present input invariant moves the nonforward value from $0.588$ to $0.378\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$. Dense momentum-space surfaces and finite-transfer-window phase-space maps show the structure this freedom controls. The tensor-network organization is chosen with composition in mind. The same shared subunits, operator hierarchy, and qualification protocol extend to the neutron, the spin-1 deuteron, and spin-$3/2$ nuclei, where the number of symmetry and exchange constraints grows quickly and a structural representation becomes the practical route. The quantum circuits are verified feature maps and state encodings; their capacity and cost are measured alongside the classical blocks.

papers.title: MAGI (Multivariate Autoencoder for particle Generative Inference): a generative Machine Learning framework for accelerated multi-stage particle simulations
papers.abstract: Monte Carlo particle simulations are hindered by the computational cost of particle transport. This is especially true when large mass surrounds a small sensitive volume. MAGI is a conditional variational autoencoder that learns the joint energy, position and direction distribution of particles crossing a closed surface in a multi-stage simulation, to be resampled and re-injected in a smaller mass model. We validated it generating crossings, variables describing particle features later in the simulation, injecting them into the same Geant4 mass model and comparing the spectrum and counts at detector level with full simulation. Rates per injected crossing agree with unity at $\sim1σ$ on our benchmark models. We measure the gain of MAGI with statistical amplification $1/χ$ and computational speed-up $S$: the first goes from 150 for high-statistics cosmic rays to 12000 for rare radioactive decays, while the latter ranges from 2.1 to almost 240, depending on source type and mass model. These first results validate MAGI v1.0.0 released on GitHub.

papers.title: Deep Unrolling of Lanczos-based Laplacian Eigensolver for Crop Classification in Satellite Images
papers.abstract: Per-pixel crop classification in satellite images is an important pre-processing step in remote crop monitoring. Leveraging progress in signed graph signal processing, we build an interpretable and lightweight neural network for binary crop classification (e.g., corn versus non-corn) in two stages: i) learn a signed graph from data, and ii) unroll a Lanczos-based eigensolver to compute the eigenvector $\u_1$ associated with the smallest eigenvalue of a hybrid graph Laplacian $\cL$ for spectral clustering. Specifically, we first construct a near-balanced signed graph $\cG^s$, where signed edge weights $w_{i,j}\in(-1,1)$ are computed from learned feature distances $d_{i,j}$ via a hyperbolic tangent mapping. Given $\cG^s$, we estimate $\u_1$ by unrolling the Lanczos algorithm and use $\mathrm{sign}(\u_1)$ for binary classification. Mathematically, we develop a theorem establishing conditions under which $\u_1$ can be well approximated after finite Lanczos iterations. Motivated by this theorem, we relax the classical Lanczos orthogonality constraints during unrolling and optimize end-to-end classification performance while promoting the derived conditions for accurate eigenvector approximation. Experiments on real-world Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel imagery show classification performance comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning models while reducing parameters by up to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: The Rebundling of Freelance Work in the AI Age
papers.abstract: This paper examines how freelance work is changing in the AI era. We compare the activities people undertake in ChatGPT with the work clients request on Upwork, an online freelance platform, and examine how clients combine tasks into projects. We find that activities more prevalent in ChatGPT tend to lose marketplace share on Upwork, while those less prevalent tend to gain share. Within AI-related work, demand is becoming more diverse, and job postings combine tasks that were rarely requested together before the generative AI era. AI-related postings also have substantially larger project budgets and involve more hours of work, while differences in hourly rates are small. Together, these findings suggest that AI is reshaping not only which tasks clients outsource, but also how they combine tasks into larger, higher-value projects.

papers.title: Relativistic Second Random-Phase Approximation: Formalism and Applications to Giant Resonances
papers.abstract: We develop a self-consistent relativistic second random-phase approximation (RSRPA) based on covariant energy density functional with density dependent point-coupling interaction. The formalism extends the conventional simple configuration space composed of particle-hole ($p$-$h$) transitions by including two-particle-two-hole ($2p$-$2h$) configurations through a generalized Thouless ansatz and a time-dependent variational principle. To ensure consistency with the underlying mean-field ground state and avoid the double counting of correlations, we implement the subtraction method, in which the static contribution is removed from the residual interaction. The first applications of the RSRPA include studies of isoscalar and isovector giant monopole (ISGMR and IVGMR) and quadrupole resonances (ISGQR and IVGQR) in $^{16}$O, which demonstrate the importance of $2p$-$2h$ couplings to describe the fragmentation of the transition strength and the stabilizing role of the subtraction method.

papers.title: Beyond Foreign-Key Connectivity: Semantic Relationship Representation for Relational Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Relational databases encode information through tables and primary--foreign key constraints. Although recent Relational Deep Learning (RDL) approaches represent these databases as heterogeneous graphs, a foreign-key connection primarily specifies structural connectivity between records. Its semantic interpretation may involve additional information that is not explicitly represented by connectivity alone. This paper introduces a conceptual framework for constructing relationship-aware representations from relational databases. The framework distinguishes three complementary aspects: (i) schema-defined relationship semantics, including endpoint types and foreign-key roles; (ii) association entities and explicitly available relationship-level attributes; and (iii) contextual information describing the temporal and structural circumstances of a connection. We formulate a Relationship Representation Construction (RRC) protocol that maps relational schema elements and database records to node representations, relationship descriptors, and contextual representations. A key principle of the protocol is semantic ownership: attributes are assigned to records, relationships, or context according to their meaning, rather than merely their physical location in a database table.
