Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.

papers.title: A minimal intuitionistic public announcement logic
papers.abstract: We introduce intuitionistic public announcement logics Lmin and Lequ determined by classes of birelational frames where the intuitionistic preorder and the modal accessibility relation do not need to satisfy the confluence conditions traditionally considered within the framework of IPAL. Our logics can be seen as generalisations of IPAL seeing that their language is based on a binary epistemic modality of "relativised knowledge" that allows us to define valid reduction axioms. Our main results are the soundness and completeness of Lmin with respect to the class of all birelational frames and the soundness and completeness of Lequ with respect to the class of all birelational frames where the modal accessibility relation is an equivalence relation.

papers.title: Causal Concept Explanations for Deep Neural Models
papers.abstract: Concept-based explanations in neural models are important for the development, certification, and adoption of autonomous systems. Yet, interpretability remains correlational. Without methods to guide and quantify causal relationships between explanations, a concept explanation can be provided without being necessary or sufficient for the observed output thereby appearing correct while misleading. We introduce Causal Concept Wrapper Network (CCW-Net), the first use of interventional mediation analysis from fields such as economics, medicine, and epidemiology as a training objective to align causal effects of concept-based explanations with a model's output. We further apply mediation analysis as an evaluation tool to quantify, per concept label combination, how much of any model's output is causally attributable to each concept explanation. As a training objective, CCW-Net shapes a model's concept representations such that they are both necessary and sufficient for the outputs they are credited with and independent of other concepts' contributions. Counterfactual concept representations anchor a set of causal alignment criteria: necessity, sufficiency, and independence. Necessity drives irrelevant concept effects toward zero, sufficiency ensures relevant concept representations fully reconstruct a model's output, and independence enforces the total effect decomposes linearly across concepts. We evaluate CCW-Net across aircraft control, driving, and image classification. CCW-Net provides a step toward concept-based explanations that are not merely interpretable, but quantifiably causal, supporting safer evaluation, certification, and deployment of transparent and trustworthy neural models.

papers.title: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes
authors: Jean-Louis de Bougrenet de la Tocnaye
papers.abstract: The theory of turbo iterative decoding was brought into the quantum coding framework through the development of quantum serial turbo codes and quantum block turbo codes. In this paper, we present a theory for multidimensional quantum block turbo codes, a turbo decoding technique for multi layer product codes. We describe its algorithm and simulate the performance for the 3D case on a depolarizing channel.

papers.title: Good Practices for Measuring the Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction by Brillouin Light Scattering and Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect
papers.abstract: The interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) is a key ingredient for stabilizing chiral magnetic states, such as skyrmions and chiral domain walls, which are key building blocks for next-generation spintronic technologies. Despite its importance, the quantitative determination of the iDMI constant, $D$, is often plagued by significant discrepancies. This paper establishes a set of good practices for measuring iDMI using two primary techniques: Brillouin Light Scattering (BLS) and the Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE). Through the analysis of Co/Pt-based heterostructures, this work provides a comprehensive roadmap for measurement procedures, data evaluation, and uncertainty analysis. Our analysis highlights the crucial role of magnetic parameters used to extract the iDMI constant and propagation of their uncertainties, and the measurement model for enhancing measurement reliability. The proposed methodology provides a practical framework for improving the consistency and reproducibility of iDMI measurements across different laboratories and experimental techniques.

papers.title: Bi-Hamiltonian structure and conserved quantities of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell system
papers.abstract:
We study the Hamiltonian and bi-Hamiltonian structure of the Yajima-Oikawa-Newell (YON) system, an integrable model of long wave-short wave interaction depending on two real parameters $α$ and $β$, which reduces to the Yajima-Oikawa system for $α=0$ and to the Newell system for $β=0$. For $α
eq0$, a constant shift of the long wave maps the YON system into the Newell system, for which two nonlocal Hamiltonian operators are known. We show that, for $α
eq0$, the system admits no local Hamiltonian operator homogeneous in its natural grading and polynomial in $β$. A nonlocal gauge transformation built on the potential of the long wave makes the first of the known operators local for a single value of its parameter: the transformed system is Hamiltonian, for every $α
eq0$ and every $β$, with respect to a local, non-degenerate Poisson operator, which is the Lie-Poisson structure of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ current algebra. From a recursion operator advancing the hierarchy by two steps, given in explicit weakly nonlocal form, we construct a second, weakly nonlocal Hamiltonian structure, whose nonlocal tail is generated by the three autonomous Lie point symmetries of the system, and prove that both structures are compatible. Since the recursion operator admits no square root and the first structure has no Casimirs, the Lenard-Magri chain splits into two families, seeded by the two simplest conserved quantities. Every flow of both families is local, and all the corresponding Hamiltonians are in involution. As by-products, we relate the Lie point symmetries of the system to its conserved quantities via Noether's theorem, and obtain the conserved densities in closed form by asymptotic diagonalisation of the Lax pair.

papers.title: Scattering thresholds for the NLS equation with polynomially decaying damping
papers.abstract: We study the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a linear damping of strength $a(1+t)^{-θ}$, where $a>0$ and $θ\ge0$, in the whole energy-subcritical range. For $θ>0$, the time-averaged damping vanishes, so that the scattering theory developed in our previous work does not apply. We show that the long-time dynamics is governed by the time integrability of an effective coupling, which decays faster than any power when $θ<1$, polynomially when $θ=1$, and not at all when $θ>1$. In the mass-subcritical case, all solutions are global. They scatter when $θ<1$ and, for $θ=1$, above an explicit exponent depending on $a$. On the other hand, no non-trivial solution is asymptotically free below a second explicit exponent when $θ=1$, and below the short-range exponent $1+2/N$ when $θ>1$. In the mass-critical case, solutions are global below the ground state. Moreover, for $θ\le1$, every solution which survives until its decaying mass becomes subcritical is global and scatters. In the intercritical case, we prove small data scattering and, for $θ\le1$, a dichotomy between scattering and grow-up of the gradient. Finally, in the scale-invariant case $θ=1$, we analyze the range between the two thresholds. We reduce the equation exactly to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a decaying repulsive harmonic potential, and we construct approximate solitary waves with an integrable error. This leads to a conjecture, supported by numerical simulations, on the sharpness of the scattering threshold.

papers.title: Canonical Volumes of Threefolds with Positive Geometric Genus
papers.abstract: We prove that a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus has canonical volume at least $1/30$, with strict inequality when its Euler characteristic is positive. We describe the equality cases as canonical hypersurfaces of degree $28$ in $\mathbb P(1,3,4,5,14)$. These canonical models and their smooth projective resolutions are simply connected. Their coarse moduli space is irreducible and rational of dimension $103$, with finite quotient singularities; all admissible $\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein deformations are unobstructed and arise by varying the equation.

papers.title: Discovering Equations for the Thermodynamics of South Asian Monsoon Precipitation
papers.abstract: South Asian monsoon precipitation depends on the thermodynamic structure of the lower troposphere, but how its ingredients combine to shape precipitation remains unclear, partly because this dependence is nonlocal in the vertical. We use symbolic distillation, which combines neural networks and symbolic regression, to discover interpretable precipitation equations from 21 years of June-August reanalysis data. Neural networks first learn the vertical thermodynamic structure most relevant to precipitation, condensing each variable into a single interpretable feature not tied to a particular vertical grid. Then, symbolic regression derives closed-form equations from these features and the surface state. Our best equation explains 1.5 times as much precipitation variance as a widely used buoyancy-based diagnostic and recovers about 85% of neural network skill while using about a thousand times fewer parameters. Unlike the buoyancy diagnostic, which adds moisture and instability, the equations treat them as competing controls, with the heaviest precipitation occurring when the lower free troposphere is humid. Over ocean, sensible heating is associated with additional precipitation mainly when near-surface air is warm and moist, improving predicted precipitation and its diurnal cycle. Although the learned features were optimized only for precipitation prediction, the equations largely respond to each feature as expected from convective physics, consistent with the reanalysis. These responses reduce the dependence of monsoon precipitation on the entire vertical column to a few simple, testable constraints that could guide data-driven precipitation models to make them more physically consistent.

papers.title: The strongly local part of nonlinear Dirichlet structures and its energy measures
papers.abstract: This paper substantially extends the results of Sasaya (2026, JFA): we propose a framework for nonlinear generalizations of regular Dirichlet forms and prove that each energy in this framework has a largest strongly local part. We also prove the existence and uniqueness of canonical energy measures of this part, which satisfy convexity and locality properties and, under additional assumptions, certain chain rules in one variable. In particular, our framework requires neither $p$-homogeneity nor strong locality. Moreover, under a Ball--Carlen--Lieb-type upper bound, we prove more detailed chain rules for the directional derivatives of these energy measures. Our framework is applicable both to $p$-energy forms on fractals and to a class of symmetric nonlinear Dirichlet forms in the sense of Cipriani and Grillo~\cite{CG2003}, including those of Orlicz--Sobolev and variable-exponent Sobolev type.

papers.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by having a draft model propose multiple tokens for the target model to verify in one pass. The speedup is governed by the expected acceptance length (EAL), yet standard training objectives such as cross-entropy, KL divergence, and total variation focus only on distribution matching or single-step overlap. Recent studies instead propose block-level training objectives, aiming to optimize EAL directly. However, these objectives remain surrogates rather than exact formulations of EAL. For example, some average later acceptance over target-distributed continuations rather than the verification branches selected by accepted tokens, introducing a covariance gap that can reverse the gradient direction. We analyze this gap and derive REAL, a real EAL training loss that uses path weights for unbiased estimation and Rao-Blackwellization for variance reduction. In a controlled loss-level comparison with a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B target and a Domino drafter, REAL outperforms WTV, VSD, DBLast, and the static LK baseline on probabilistic serving acceptance length across 9 task subsets and 5 evaluation seeds. These gains require only a change to the training loss, with no modification to the drafter architecture or inference procedure, demonstrating the practicality of real EAL training. A reference implementation of the REAL loss is available at https://github.com/King-ty/speculators/tree/real-loss.

papers.title: Simulating closed- and open-system dynamics of Tavis--Cummings lattices on fault-tolerant quantum computers
papers.abstract: Tavis--Cummings lattices couple cavities containing several emitters and host polaritonic many-body dynamics whose real-time correlations are costly to compute classically in two dimensions, especially when unequal emitter relaxation or dephasing rates break permutation symmetry. We analyze logical resources for fault-tolerant closed- and open-system simulation of an atom-resolved lattice with $L$ cavities, $N$ emitters per cavity, and photon cutoff $n\_{\max}$, including target observable estimation. Building on ladder-operator block encoding, we construct circuits for photon hopping and local light--matter exchange and combine them to encode the lattice Hamiltonian. By updating source and destination photon occupations in place, the hopping circuit eliminates the auxiliary $L\lceil\log_2(n\_{\max}+1)\rceil$-qubit photon register used by two-register implementations. Across three uniform-coefficient examples with $16$ to $256$ cavities, the controlled walk uses $4.75$--$8.11%$ fewer Toffoli gates than the paired two-register implementation under matched shared preparation, precision, control, and workspace conventions. For closed systems, we implement real-time evolution with generalized quantum signal processing and bound the cost of estimating retarded cavity spectral functions. For open systems with photon loss, emitter relaxation, and dephasing, we use a sampled first-order dilation and bound the runs and timesteps needed to estimate transient photon statistics such as $g^{(2)}(0)$. With state-preparation and measurement costs explicit, these estimates provide a reference for assessing fault-tolerant light--matter lattice simulation costs.

papers.title: A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA)
papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is the de facto method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks, achieving strong task adaptation with minimal trainable parameters and low optimization cost. Beyond this efficiency, practitioners have observed two striking properties: \textit{robustness to catastrophic forgetting} and the ability to \textit{merge independently trained adapters} into a single model that performs competitively across multiple tasks. These properties are central to continual and multi-task learning, yet remain poorly understood. In this work, we provide a theoretical explanation through a unified \textit{margin-based perspective}. We analyze LoRA in multiclass linear classification under a near-orthogonal task regime with $\ell_2$-regularization, and characterize the optimal LoRA adapter across regularization regimes. Our analysis shows that, in an intermediate regime of regularization parameters, the optimal adapter aligns with the \emph{max-margin solution} on the fine-tuning data. Building on this characterization, we derive two key consequences. First, we obtain closed-form expressions for the margins on pre-training and fine-tuning data, revealing a precise margin trade-off: the regularization parameter controls the balance between retention and adaptation. Second, we analyze adapter merging, proving that merged models achieve positive margin on each task and deriving optimal mixing coefficients that balance margins across tasks and maximize the margin over their union. These results lead to a simple, training-free merging rule, which we term \textit{margin-based LoRA merging} (MaLoRA). Experiments on modern architectures and real datasets validate our theoretical predictions, showing that MaLoRA matches or outperforms several adapter-merging baselines across a range of vision and language classification tasks.

papers.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
papers.abstract: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.

papers.title: Improved Myelin Water Fraction Estimation and Uncertainty Mapping in Multicomponent T2 Relaxometry via NNLS Bootstrap Aggregation
papers.abstract: Estimating the myelin water fraction (MWF) from multicomponent T2 relaxometry requires solving an ill-conditioned inverse problem, making estimates sensitive to noise. Regularization can improve stability but may introduce bias. Conventional NNLS-based methods also provide point estimates without directly quantifying voxelwise variability. To address these limitations, we propose the non-negative least squares Bootstrap Barycenter (NNLS-BB), combining residual resampling with repeated NNLS reconstruction. We average spectra and derived parameters across bootstrap replicates and use their standard deviations to characterize sensitivity to signal perturbations. The method requires neither an explicit spectral regularization penalty nor a training dataset. NNLS-BB was evaluated on 40,000 simulated voxels with signal-to-noise ratios of 50-1000, against conventional NNLS, two regularized NNLS methods, and a model-informed machine-learning (MIML) method. Scan-rescan repeatability was assessed across 20 white-matter regions in two independent cohorts comprising 13 healthy participants. NNLS-BB achieved the lowest MWF mean absolute error and root mean squared error in all simulated noise regimes. Mean absolute error decreased by 36-41% relative to conventional NNLS, alongside lower error dispersion. Compared with Bayes-Reg-$D^{-1}$ and MIML, NNLS-BB achieved comparable dispersion but substantially lower bias, although MIML reconstructed the full spectrum more accurately. In vivo, NNLS-BB yielded the lowest regional scan-rescan dispersion and highest mean correlation in both cohorts. Bootstrap standard-deviation maps provided complementary information about parameter variability. These results support residual-bootstrap aggregation for improving MWF estimation while providing voxelwise variability maps from a single acquisition.

papers.title: On operators with infinitely many spectral components
papers.abstract: For a unital complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb N}\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$. We prove that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing$ if and only if $\mathscr A$ contains a sequence of non-zero pairwise orthogonal idempotents, and that the number of components of a spectrum is always finite, $\aleph_0$ or $\mathfrak c$. This allows us to extend the spectral depth $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ to a cardinal-valued invariant with values in $\mathbb N\cup\{\aleph_0,\mathfrak c\}$. We show that $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ precisely when $\mathscr A$ contains a dyadic family of idempotents indexed by the full binary tree. In that case, some element has spectrum homeomorphic to the Cantor space $\mathbf 2^{\mathbb N}$. The supremum defining $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ is attained when the spectral classes of $\mathscr A$ are dense and when $\mathscr A$ is commutative, but not in general. We construct a unital complex Banach algebra with $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ and $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr A)=\varnothing$. If $Δ$ is the character space of a commutative $\mathscr A$ and $π_0(Δ)$ is the space of all components of $Δ$, then $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\card\bigl(π_0(Δ)\bigr)$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is finite, $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\aleph_0$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is infinite and scattered, and $d_σ(\mathscr A)=\mathfrak c$ when $π_0(Δ)$ is not scattered. We also prove that the spectral depth is additive with respect to finite direct sums and that the spectral classes are invariant under injective holomorphic functions.

papers.title: Cost controllability and predictive control of input-constrained monotone systems on Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: Cost controllability, relating controllability and a performance measure like the stage cost in model predictive control (MPC), is a key tool in the stability and suboptimality analysis of closed-loop systems. We establish cost controllability for maximal monotone control systems subject to input constraints, a class encompassing finite- and infinite-dimensional port-Hamiltonian systems with colocated input and output. To this end, we employ a recently proposed saturated feedback to derive state-dependent bounds on the closed-loop cost. Our main result is that cost controllability holds globally with semiglobal exponential rate. We first establish this result in continuous time and then extend it to sampled-data systems. Whereas a qualitative detectability-like property is sufficient for asymptotic convergence of the controller, cost controllability requires quantitative rates. We provide two verifiable conditions ensuring cost controllability with explicit exponential rates: coercivity of the sum of system operator and output injection, and exponential detectability of the linear part. Moreover, under the coercivity condition, the resulting MPC scheme without terminal conditions renders the equilibrium globally asymptotically stable with semiglobal exponential rate already for prediction horizon two. We illustrate our results by a nonlinear finite-dimensional system, a semilinear heat equation and a nonlinearly damped wave equation.

papers.title: Phragmén-Lindelöf theorems for parabolic equations of p-laplacian-type
papers.abstract: We consider rigidity properties of ancient solutions to parabolic equations of $p$-Laplacian-type. We start with the degenerate range $p>2$. First, a solution which is bounded above in an intrinsic backward paraboloid is either bounded in an entire half-space, or grows in space at least like a power with a sharp, explicit exponent. This relies on the expansion of positivity and on the Comparison Principle. Then, we turn to the growth in time. Positivity in the paraboloid alone yields no upper rate: we present explicit self-similar solutions, positive in the paraboloid, with $u(0,-T)\simeq T^β$ for every $β\le0$ and every $β\ge1$. For solutions bounded below in the paraboloid, we prove a dichotomy for the infimum of $u(\cdot,-T)$ on a ball whose radius is a fixed fraction of that of the paraboloid at time $-T$: either it is of order $T$ along a sequence of times, or it grows sublinearly, like $T^ζ$ with $ζ<1$ explicit. In the second case, a Harnack-type argument shows that the supremum on the same ball grows at most linearly. Then, we carry out the same program in the singular, supercritical range $\frac{2N}{N+1}<p<2$, where the picture is similar but several roles are reversed. In space, the iteration via the Comparison Principle can only be started from a point lying above an explicit slope, and explicit solutions show that nothing better than a cone bound can be expected below it. The self-similar profiles are unique but only local, and positivity in the paraboloid is compatible with every exponent $β\le1$ and with no exponent in $(1,\frac1{2-p})$. In time, the dichotomy is replaced by an a priori linear bound for the infimum. Similarities and differences between the two ranges are collected at the end of the work.

papers.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
papers.abstract: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. This architecture provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. We achieve a median reset time constant of approximately 48 ns for the $|g\rangle-|e\rangle$ transition, with an effective bath temperature of 30 mK. A 400-ns reset pulse yields residual excited-state populations of $0.29\%$ and $0.67\%$ for qubits initialized in $|g\rangle$ and $|e\rangle$, respectively. We further demonstrate efficient leakage removal from the $|f\rangle$ state, reducing its residual population to $0.51\%$. These results establish a simple, reproducible, and easy-to-integrate approach to dissipation engineering in superconducting quantum processors.

papers.title: Pseudoconformal characterizations of scattering in weighted Sobolev spaces for non-scaling-invariant mass-subcritical NLS
papers.abstract: We consider mass-subcritical nonlinear Schrödinger equations with finitely many power-type nonlinearities and initial data in weighted Sobolev spaces. In the short-range regime, we prove a pseudoconformal characterization of scattering in the weighted energy space $Σ$. We also establish a fractional counterpart in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1)$, formulated in terms of the boundedness of the order-$s$ pseudoconformal operator. Our results include equations with combined nonlinearities, for which no distinguished scaling symmetry is available. As an application of the fractional theory, we prove small-data scattering in $Σ^s$, $s\in(0,1]$. The arguments rely on the lens transformation, harmonic-oscillator Strichartz estimates, and fractional harmonic Sobolev estimates.

papers.title: Evaluating Tactile Encoding Strategies for Communicating 3-D Shape
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional haptic displays, such as programmable pin arrays and vibrotactile or friction-modulating touchscreens, enable tactile communication of complex shapes in a low-profile form factor. However, many shapes of interest, including CAD models, three-dimensional graphs, and map topographies, are inherently three-dimensional. This work investigates two methods for encoding 3-D information using a 2-D tactile display: (1) a single tactile height map providing coarse but quantifiable depth cues, and (2) a series of binary layers communicating sequential slices of a 3-D model, supporting more complex geometries such as overhangs and cavities. We further compare performance across two display types--a friction-modulating display and a pin array--to examine how the level of haptic abstraction affects users' ability to decode discrete 3-D information. A user study demonstrates that participants were able to effectively complete a 3-D assembly task using both strategies, achieving high accuracy across all display types. While the pin array supported faster task completion and higher-rated--though not statistically significant--user experience than the friction-modulating display for the binary-layer task, these differences did not translate to significant differences in overall usability (i.e., reassembly accuracy success). Together, these results identify design trade-offs and inform development of future surface haptic displays that support the communication and interpretation of discrete 3-D information in tactile graphics.

papers.title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
papers.abstract: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969. Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) still show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD. Regge exchange organizes the fragmentation region in triple-Regge form. It supplies the diffractive mass law of the excited systems, with the shrinkage of the Pomeron in its transfer dependence. Finite-energy sum rules and the two-component duality of Harari and Freund equate averaged towers of resonances with that exchange. Duality therefore motivates describing the excited systems in hadronic degrees of freedom. The review follows the cascade description through its predecessors, namely the fireballs of Niu, the novas of Jacob and Slansky, the clusters of Hwa, Good-Walker diffraction, and the two-stage dissociation of Hama. HEART (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions) assembles these pieces into an event-level cascade of two-body hadronic transitions. A companion paper (arXiv:2611.11570) defines it and tests it against the NA49 data. The review closes with the fragmentation-region measurements that would separate a resonance cascade from a string, namely the isospin of forward baryons, the local balance of strangeness in associated production, and forward resonance signals with their mass tails.

papers.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have emerged as effective alternatives to autoregressive models for latency-critical tasks, enabling faster token generation. Recent advances employ block diffusion with self-editing capabilities, where each block refines tokens iteratively before advancing to the next one. Yet each block is only as fast as its slowest token, and the next block cannot start before it. We suggest Blurring the Block Boundaries (B3), a novel method with which two blocks are refined in parallel within a shared forward pass. B3 calibrates itself on the fly, opening the next block only once the model is ready to start generating it. It is a training-free and hyperparameter-free acceleration method which seamlessly integrates within any self-editing block diffusion model. Evaluated on state-of-the-art DLMs across 10 diverse datasets spanning varied tasks and difficulty levels, B3 results in on par generation quality and 11.5-14.5% speedup compared to the base model, pushing the Pareto frontier for latency-quality trade-offs in DLM inference.

papers.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.

papers.title: Semiparametric Inference in Panel Data with Interactive and High-dimensional Confounding
papers.abstract: This paper develops inference for a low-dimensional treatment coefficient in partially linear panel models with high-dimensional observed covariates and latent interactive confounding. Flexible adjustment for observed covariates can leave correlated factor components in treatment and outcome residuals, invalidating standard double/debiased machine learning (DML). We propose Factor-Augmented DML (FA-DML), which estimates treatment-side and reduced-form factor spaces from first-stage residuals. The estimator combines a feasible double projection with three-fold, unit-level cross-fitting. The double projection controls interactions between the two estimated factor spaces. The separate folds eliminate same-training-unit pairings in the leading disturbance components of the factor-estimation errors. Under fixed factor ranks, pervasive factor signals, strict exogeneity, and joint asymptotics in the number of units N and periods T , FA-DML is first-order equivalent to an infeasible oracle, is asymptotically normal, and admits consistent variance estimation. In the baseline simulation design with strong interactive confounding, FA-DML confidence intervals have coverage close to the nominal level. Standard DML and a two-fold variant that estimates both factor spaces on the same units substantially undercover. In an application to U.S. states, FA-DML finds that a 10% increase in the real minimum wage is associated with a roughly 1.1% lower 50/10 wage ratio. The estimate is stable across control sets and first-stage learners.

papers.title: Tolerance complexes of chordal graphs and squarefree symbolic powers
papers.abstract: For a simplicial complex $K$ and an integer $t\ge0$, the $t$-tolerance complex $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ consists of the sets that become faces of $K$ after deleting at most $t$ of their elements. Kim and Lew conjectured that if $K$ is $d$-Leray, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(η(d+1,t+1)-1)$-Leray (the Leray conjecture), and that if $K$ is $d$-collapsible, then $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is $(η(d+1,t+1)-1)$-collapsible (the collapsibility conjecture), where $η$ is the Erdős--Gallai number. We prove the collapsibility conjecture for $d=1$ when $t\le3$ or $\dim K\le4$, and for all $t$ when $K$ is the clique complex of a subtree graph of a spider, a class of chordal graphs containing all interval and split graphs; in particular, it holds for nerves of finite families of intervals. For every $d$, we prove both conjectures when $K$ has at most $d+1$ facets, when $K$ has nonzero homology in its top dimension, and when the Stanley--Reisner ideal of $K$ is squarefree stable. The Stanley--Reisner ideal of $\mathcal{T}_t(K)$ is the $(t+1)$-st squarefree symbolic power of that of $K$, so the Leray conjecture becomes a regularity bound. Using this, we prove the Leray conjecture for flag complexes when $t\le3$, and for all $t$ for independence complexes of bipartite and chordal graphs, and we show that it is preserved under joins. We also construct chordal graphs $H$ for which the Leray number of $\mathcal{T}_t(\mathrm{Cl}(H))$ exceeds its Helly dimension by an arbitrarily large amount, and others for which it depends on the field. Finally, we reduce the case $t=1$ of the Leray bound for $d$-collapsible complexes to a question on intersections of links.

papers.title: An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) define a distribution through a scalar energy, $p_θ(x)\propto\exp(-E_θ(x))$, and are usually presented as one model family among many. This tutorial has a broader goal: beyond introducing EBMs, it uses them as a single lens that connects the different aspects of machine learning. Any EBM is specified by three choices, the energy, which determines what the model represents; the inference procedure, which samples from or optimizes the energy; and the learning method, which fits the energy to data. We first develop these components, including sampling, variational inference, and learning by maximum likelihood, noise contrastive estimation, pseudolikelihood, score matching, and adversarial training, and show that the learning methods share one contrastive structure. We then show that discriminative models, generative models such as GANs, normalizing flows, diffusion and autoregressive models, representation learning methods such as contrastive learning, word2vec, BERT, denoising auto-encoders, and diffusion representations, reinforcement learning with EBM policies and world models, inverse reinforcement learning, and planning, as well as inference-time computation with verifiers, are all EBMs that differ in these three choices, mostly in how they handle the partition function and sampling. This view explains existing methods, organizes them into a common framework, and suggests new algorithms by replacing one component while keeping the others, with composition of energies as a principled way to combine learned models at inference time.

papers.title: Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly exhibit capabilities that resemble human Learning by Thinking (LbT), the acquisition of new insight through internal processes such as explanation and reasoning, without new external input. A systematic account of the cognitive mechanisms behind these capabilities, and of their limits, remains underdeveloped. This paper proposes a Cognitive LbT Framework that maps four mechanisms (Reflective Reasoning, Synthetic Memory Formation, Internal Simulation, and Conceptual Self-Organization) onto computational processes in LLMs. Drawing on representative methods, including chain-of-thought prompting, self-consistency, self-reflection, Tree-of-Thoughts search, Self-Instruct, and self-taught reasoning, the analysis argues that selected methods can functionally approximate aspects of these mechanisms and can improve performance on some tasks without additional labeled examples, although this does not always constitute durable learning in model parameters. For example, Self-Instruct generated approximately 52,000 instructions from 175 seed tasks and reported a 33% absolute improvement on Super-NaturalInstructions (Y. Wang et al., 2023). The same mechanisms also produce characteristic failures, including hallucination diffusion, model collapse, concept drift, and high computational cost. These failures are not isolated technical defects but follow from four structural asymmetries between LLMs and human cognition: the identity of generator and monitor, closed learning loops without external grounding, symbolic rather than sensorimotor simulation, and the cost of inference-time computation. The framework yields testable propositions about when LbT in LLMs should succeed or fail and offers a structured basis for designing more reliable autonomous learning systems.

papers.title: Optimization principles, revisited
papers.abstract: The brain solves a wide range of problems, and some of these solutions are very good indeed. It is an old idea that, in some cases, these solutions may be as good as possible given the relevant constraints. If this is true we can promote this notion of optimization to a principle from which aspects of function and mechanism can be derived, ideally with no free parameters. Optimization principles are powerful and have had many successes, but they remain controversial. We start with a reminder of a classic example---diffraction limited optics in insect eyes---and then a summary of why you should worry about optimization as a more general principle. Next we turn to recent progress on the theory of optimal motion estimation in fly vision, and finally summarize recent results on the landscape for optimization, arguing that (contrary to widely held intuitions) optimal performance need not require the underlying mechanisms to have finely tuned parameters. I hope to convince you that this is a moment to take optimization seriously as the basis for theories of neural coding and computation. This is based on a rather informal lecture at the summer school LASCON X in Sao Paulo, and I have tried to preserve that tone here; pointers are given to more detailed and technical discussions.

papers.title: What Factors Matter for Collection-Level Counting with Human-AI Collaboration?
papers.abstract: Many scientific and policy decisions require estimating the total number of target objects across a large image collection. Exhaustive human labeling is often infeasible, while raw model predictions can be biased, especially under domain shift. Recent human-AI estimation methods combine imperfect model predictions with limited human verification to obtain reliable collection-level estimates. However, existing work provides little guidance on how practitioners should choose among models, estimators, and adaptation strategies for a new deployment. We study these choices within a common human-in-the-loop counting framework across 12 tasks spanning biomedical microscopy, ground-level and aerial wildlife surveys, and overhead imagery of urban structures. Our results show that modern multimodal models provide a strong, training-free starting point for many tasks, while fine-tuned detectors become more advantageous at larger labeling budgets and across repeated deployments. Estimation efficiency improves further when model predictions are used to prioritize which units humans label, rather than sampling uniformly. We also find that each model's ranking quality can be estimated with a small pilot set, yielding practical guidance for selecting strategies on new counting tasks. In a field deployment on aerial pronghorn surveys, a task-specific adaptation of these methods meets the survey's $\pm 5\%$ tolerance after reviewing a median of only $3.2\%$ of collected images.

papers.title: Complexity of Deciding Existence of Maltsev Polymorphisms of Finite Relational Structures
papers.abstract: In this article, we show that the problem of deciding whether a finite relational structure $\mathbf{A}$ admits a Maltsev polymorphism is a computational problem, which can be solved in polynomial time. We provide a proof of this result by reducing the problem to deciding whether a binary relational structure, associated with $\mathbf{A}$ admits such a polymorphism. In our construction of such an algorithm, we make an extensive use of a property of binary relations, which is implied by the existence of a Maltsev polymorphism, the so-called rectangularity property.

papers.title: Parabolic semiinfinite sheaves on affine flag varieties
papers.abstract: We study sheaves on affine flag varieties of reductive algebraic groups in parabolic semiinfinite settings, generalizing some constructions and results from the work of Gaitsgory and of Achar, Dhillon, and the first author (for the case of the Borel subgroup) and of Dhillon and Lysenko (for characteristic-$0$ coefficients and a particular case of parabolic semiinfinite condition). In particular we define perverse t-structures and Raskin equivalences in this context, and study an analogue of the Gaitsgory sheaf. In future work, these $\infty$-categories will be related to representation-theoretic $\infty$-categories associated with the Langlands dual group.

papers.title: Stochastic Discrete Variable Representation: Tensor Network Eigenstates on General Potential Energy Surfaces
papers.abstract: Tensor network states such as tree tensor network states (TTNS) or matrix product states (MPS) allow very compact representations of high-dimensional wave functions. Using them efficiently relies on a compact representation of the Hamiltonian, and many methods are limited to the sum-of-products (SOP) form. General potential energy surfaces (PESs) do not have this form. To overcome this issue, a stochastic discrete variable representation (SDVR) is presented. The matrix elements of the potential operator in the node-local basis are estimated stochastically by importance sampling of grid configurations. The estimator of the matrix elements is unbiased, and the PES is only evaluated pointwise. The variance is reduced by representing parts of the potential with a 2-mode representation and only sampling the remainder. Sampling noise biases the eigenvalues. A noise-control scheme mitigates this bias. Final energies are obtained from an unbiased variational Monte Carlo estimator. The method is demonstrated by calculating vibrational states of CH3 (6D) and acetonitrile (12D), as well as the zero-point vibrational energy of uracil (30D). For all three systems, the energies agree with the exact references to sub-wavenumber accuracy.

papers.title: Operational limits of reference renewal for retained quantum-service results
papers.abstract: We implement reference renewal to reconsider retained physical quantum-service results under a prespecified protocol. Twelve transitions retained six results each; ten completed renewal, eight met the prespecified endpoint, and five succeeded using retained results alone. The exact one-sided p=0.0546875 does not establish the recovery hypothesis. Incomplete references, binding failures and sequential waits expose operational limits. Offline reconstruction recovers decisions from preserved counts. Retrospective binding-plus-oracle checking accepts all 60 usable-transition results without renewal. With the exact oracle also supplying calibration scores, the study does not demonstrate incremental numerical-correctness utility of renewal.

papers.title: From Distribution of Extremes With Degradation to the Stress Redundancy Principle
papers.abstract: How a degradation source affects the statistics of the first among many identical independent stochastic particles to successfully reach a narrow target remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impact of degradation on the distributions of first-passage times and exit locations by exploiting the time-dependent fluxes associated with the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation. We also compute the escape probability by solving a mixed boundary value problem. In the large initial population $N_0$ limit, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean first passage time associated with the fastest particle, revealing how the killing field modifies the classical $1/\log(N_0)$ scaling. However, when considering the population size at the time of the first exit, we obtain a specific dependency with respect to degradation, a phenomenon that we call the stress redundancy principle. For a degradation field restricted to a narrow subregion, we use an optimal control approach to derive the optimal trajectory where the fastest escape particles will be concentrated: interestingly, we report here that the optimal trajectories avoid the degradation area depending on killing intensity. Finally, we obtain analytical expressions for the distribution of first exit points along a narrow absorbing arc in two-dimensional regular domains. In addition, for a killing subregion tangent to the target boundary, our computations reveal how geometrical parameters influence the exit distribution. In summary, a killing source can significantly affect the statistics of the fastest diffusing particles, relevant for defining cellular and molecular time scales.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Offline Reinforcement Learning with Online Action Selection Enabled by Sparse Gaussian-Process Critics
papers.abstract: Start-ups and grade changes remain largely operator-driven, while developing and maintaining dynamic models for model-based control requires substantial engineering effort. Hybrid Offline Learning and Online Optimisation (HOFLON) uses one-step offline reinforcement learning to select actions from historical transition data. In its original implementation, the online objective combines the predicted return from a tree-ensemble critic with an adversarial-autoencoder (AAE) penalty for unfamiliar state-action pairs. We examine the effect of this penalty and replace the critic and AAE with a sparse variational Gaussian-process (sGP) critic. Actions maximise $μ- κσ$, an uncertainty-adjusted estimate of the return from one action followed by the historical operating practice. On the HOFLON polymerisation-reactor benchmark, removing the AAE from HOFLON led to 4 failed start-ups in 15 runs over five critics. At its published weight, the variation in the AAE penalty is four orders of magnitude smaller than the variation in the tree-ensemble critic. Nevertheless, it changes actions when the predicted returns of competing candidates are nearly equal, and paired runs with and without the penalty diverged from the first move. With a Matérn-5/2 sGP critic, $κ= 0$ led to failure in 13 of 15 runs, whereas with $κ= 3$ none of 15 runs (five critics, three noise realisations) failed. The median and lowest returns were 13,464 and 13,398 (HOFLON: 13,393 and 12,411). A squared-exponential sGP critic with learned inducing inputs needed $κ\geq 3$ to remain within the empirical data support in steady state, and then settled with a temperature offset of 2.0 K.

papers.title: Gaussian Process-Augmented Model Predictive Contouring Control for 6-DoF Trajectory Tracking with a Holonomic AUV
papers.abstract: Small, holonomic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) enable close-range inspection of underwater structures from arbitrary viewpoints, requiring accurate position and attitude tracking under state and input constraints. Model Predictive Contouring Control (MPCC) naturally handles these requirements, but relies on an accurate dynamics model, which is difficult to obtain underwater. In this paper, we present a nonlinear MPCC in all six Degrees of Freedom (DoF) for a holonomic AUV and alleviate the inaccuracies in the dynamics by augmenting the nominal model employed with residual dynamics learned via Gaussian Process (GP) regression. The learned residual is embedded in the optimal control problem through a zero-order robust optimization scheme, which keeps the controller real-time capable at 25 Hz. A simulation ablation shows that residual selection is essential when designing the controller, and simulation and in-water experiments with the Multimodality, Observing, Low-cost, Agile (MOLA) AUV validate the resulting controllers against a nominal MPCC and a field proven Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller.

papers.title: A fast two-phase model for PEM fuel cell impedance
papers.abstract: We report a physics-based matrix model for PEM fuel cell impedance that takes into account liquid water transients in the cathode catalyst layer (CCL). This model is an extension of our previous single-phase matrix model for functionally graded CCLs. The solution to the boundary-value problem for the perturbation amplitudes is constructed from basic solutions to the respective Cauchy problem with constant coefficients on numerical cells. The single-phase model employed analytical solutions to this problem. Here, for a larger system of ODEs, the analytical solution does not exist and we used spectral decomposition of the ODE system matrix to obtain the basic solutions numerically. Our impedance model is two orders of magnitude faster than a model based on a standard, general-purpose boundary-value solver. Fitting the matrix model to an experimental spectrum takes about a minute on a laptop. The developed matrix method can be used to numerically solve high-order linear boundary-value problems with variable coefficients.

papers.title: Reliable and explainable analysis of AVS/RS by Statistical Model Checking and Process Mining
papers.abstract: Automated Vehicle Storage and Retrieval Systems (AVS/RS) are increasingly adopted to boost warehouse throughput while containing operational costs. We present an integrated analysis framework that couples discrete-event simulation with Statistical Model Checking (SMC) and Process Mining (PM) to quantify and explain AVS/RS performance. SMC, implemented through the MultiVeStA tool, delivers statistically reliable estimates of key indicators, such as cycle times, throughput, and storage utilization, across alternative stocking and picking policies with user-specified confidence levels. MultiVeStA orchestrates multiple independent simulations in a black-box manner, enabling automated verification. PM ingests the resulting event logs to uncover the behavioral patterns and bottlenecks that drive those indicators, closing the interpretability gap typical of simulation studies. We instantiate the framework on a new open-source AVS/RS simulator configured according to recent industrial guidelines and evaluate multiple control strategies. Results show that the joint use of SMC and PM enables both predictive what-if analyses and post-hoc diagnostics, providing the first combined SMC+PM assessment of AVS/RS operations and a reusable toolchain for automated warehousing research.

papers.title: The Higgs boson, naturalness, and the Universe
papers.abstract: The Higgs boson -- the only known fundamental scalar particle -- may have profound implications for both particle physics and cosmology. This review examines how the Higgs field may have influenced the Universe from its earliest moments to its present state. We first discuss particle-physics puzzles, including the naturalness and hierarchy problems, as well as the possible metastability of the electroweak vacuum. We then turn to cosmological scenarios where the Higgs boson could be a driving force, including Higgs inflation, reheating and the onset of the hot Big Bang, the electroweak phase transition, and baryogenesis via electroweak processes.

papers.title: A Bayesian approach for checking and estimating block designs in agricultural experiments
papers.abstract: Spatial blocking is a common technique used in designed agricultural experiments. Spatial blocking, however, requires important assumptions about the spatial dependence patterns in the field. Statistical models of blocked agricultural experiments often show spatial structure in the residuals, suggesting that the original model may benefit from additional assumptions regarding the spatial dependence patterns present in the field. We propose a Bayesian model for checking block membership and estimating spatial patterns missing in the original block design. Our model is particularly motivated by cases with mis-specified blocks. To accomplish this, we embed a regression tree within a Bayesian statistical model to estimate spatial effects with a block-like spatial structure. We illustrate the benefits of our model using simulated data mimicking four typical scenarios we have encountered in our applied experience in agricultural research and using two datasets generated from designed agricultural experiments. We found that our model may serve two purposes: validating the originally designed block layout, or mis-specified block-like spatial structures. Thus, our model provides researchers with a novel tool for analyzing data from designed agricultural experiments.

papers.title: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Many image classification tasks have labels that are unchanged by rotations and reflections. Equivariant quantum neural networks incorporate such symmetries by design, but the specific benefit of symmetry is difficult to isolate. Equivariant quantum circuits are usually compared with architectures that also differ in gates, structure or size. Here, we investigate the role of invariance in a controlled setting, classifying images whose labels are invariant under the dihedral group $D_4$. We compare four eight-qubit models with identical encoding, circuit structure and number of trainable parameters, and equivalent dynamical Lie algebras, and benchmark invariant implementations against non-invariant ones in terms of generalization error, robustness to shortcut learning and resilience to a realistic noise model. On four binary tasks, including MNIST and two scientific data sets of galaxies and red blood cells, the invariant models trained on a few tens of images show better generalization than non-invariant ones. Invariance also makes the models immune to orientation shortcuts: when trained with a class-dependent corner watermark, the non-invariant models learn the watermark and often drop to chance level when it is moved. We show that the gain in accuracy of invariant models persists also under a realistic noise model.

papers.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
papers.abstract: Kühnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.

papers.title: Independent Families Under Determinacy-Like Hypotheses
papers.abstract: We generalize the notion of an independent family on $ω$ to $\mathcal{J}$-independent families on an arbitrary cardinal $κ$ and then show that under determinacy-like hypotheses that there can be no such families for reasonable $\mathcal{J}$. This is quite atypical as all other generalizations of the kinds of combinatorial families coming from the theory of cardinal characteristics follow a very different pattern, which will also be explained; in this sense independent families seem particularly special. The base theory assumed throughout is $\textsf{ZF + }$All infinite sets are Dedekind infinite.

papers.title: From Video Frames to Robot Meta-Frames: A Unified Latent Interface for World Action Models
papers.abstract: Pretrained video diffusion models (VDMs) offer a powerful foundation for World Action Models (WAMs), which jointly predict robot actions and future observations. Building such models requires injecting low-dimensional robot signals (e.g. proprioception, actions, and values) into a latent space shaped by natural videos, and a key design choice is the interface through which these signals enter: existing schemes treat it as a formatting detail, spending a separate latent frame on each signal or bolting on dedicated encoders and decoders. We argue that signal injection is instead a distribution-alignment problem: how well a representation matches the prior of the pretrained VDMs during denoising. Using the relative reconstruction error of a frozen VDM denoiser as a probe, we find that conventional spatial encodings sit far off this prior, whereas frequency-domain packing yields latents that the denoiser corrects far less. Motivated by this diagnostic result, we propose MetaWAM, which folds all robot signals into a single unified meta-frame: each signal is assigned to a disjoint frequency-domain channel band and lifted to the spatial latent by an inverse DCT, yielding a decodable interface aligned with the pretrained VDM prior without any added module or architectural change. A fixed band layout together with slot-aware routing lets the same meta-frame support policy, world-model, and value prediction over a shared set of robot variables. On RoboCasa, MetaWAM reaches 68.9% success while collapsing the per-signal frames into one and cutting inference latency by 39%, and attains 85.0% success on three real-world Franka tasks. Code and models are available at https://github.com/showlab/MetaWAM

papers.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
papers.abstract: Research agents achieve increasingly strong benchmark scores, yet these scores do not necessarily translate into reliable delivery in ongoing research projects. Many research-agent benchmarks emphasize standalone tasks and relatively self-contained workflows in clean or curated workspaces. However, researchers ask agents to complete one step within an ongoing project, where requests depend on earlier session decisions and workspaces contain unfinished files, outdated versions, and failed attempts. We introduce ARE-bench to evaluate whether research agents advance ongoing projects while respecting prior decisions and existing workspace state, grounded in real session context and in-progress workspaces. ARE-bench includes 75 tasks built on agent sessions and full workspaces from recruited researchers' own projects, spanning seven research stages, 33 requirements, and 150 sub-requirements, with 1,173 binary checklist items in total. Each task is anchored at a real user request, preserves its requirements, and summarizes the earlier requests still in effect as background. The complete workspace is replayed to that boundary without cleanup, preserving artifacts from earlier turns. Each checklist is compiled from an intent-aligned rubric and credits any valid solution. Across seven frontier models, the strongest passes every checklist item on only 66.2% of tasks, and Design and Execution rank among the hardest stages for every model. Three models pass about 69% of tasks when only delivery contracts and general norms are checked, but just 28.4% to 40.0% once historical and material or workspace requirements are also checked. Evaluating delivery without these contextual requirements can therefore overestimate research agents and mask differences between them.

papers.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
papers.abstract: We investigate inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of atomic and molecular line photons as an explanation of the evolving MeV spectral feature observed by Fermi-GBM in GRB 221009A. Detections of H$α$ and Pa$α$ emission from the host galaxy motivate hydrogen recombination seeds, with only indirect support for Ly$α$. A marginal Mg XII feature in the late-time X-ray afterglow provides an event-specific motivation for metal-line seeds, whereas Si XIV, S XVI and iron K-shell transitions are motivated by historical reports of X-ray line features in other gamma-ray bursts. Strong late-time H$_2$ emission detected by the James Webb Space Telescope at the projected burst position motivates our most detailed spectral test. Assuming lateral illumination by the H$_2$ $1-0\,S(1)$ transition at $2.122\,μ{\rm m}$, we calibrate lognormal electron distributions to reproduce the observed MeV photon centroids and widths. We also require IC emission from the ultraviolet (UV) photons driving molecular fluorescence to remain compatible with contemporaneous LAT observations. In a separate test including accompanying molecular transitions, the most favourable configuration, based on the Rh3o photodissociation-region model, approximately describes the MeV feature, although all tested configurations exceed the adopted central spectral references at some energies. For an assumed precursor UV budget, favourable interception substantially reduces the seed-photon energy deficit, but even under ideal excitation and internal escape assumptions, the reference-line photon density in the compact examples falls short of the required value by factors of approximately 4-9. Collisional de-excitation, infrared photon escape and electron cooling impose additional constraints on these configurations. Atomic candidates remain kinematically possible, but their local seed-photon supply is also unestablished.

papers.title: How Well Do SAST Tools Work Across Languages? An Empirical Study Using OCPP Implementations
papers.abstract: As electric vehicle (EV) adoption accelerates globally, securing electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) software becomes increasingly critical. The Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP), widely adopted for EVCS management, places significant responsibility on developers to securely implement specifications that are subject to multiple interpretations. The variety of OCPP implementations across different programming languages provides a unique opportunity to evaluate security tooling in a real-world, multi-language context where implementation variability may introduce vulnerabilities. This study provides the first empirical evaluation of Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tool performance across multiple programming languages using OCPP implementations as a real-world test corpus. We applied both comprehensive multi-language tools (SonarQube and Semgrep) and language-specific analyzers to twelve OCPP 1.6 implementations--each written in a distinct programming language--to examine how detection patterns vary across language ecosystems. Total issues ranged from just two in Rust to 1,689 in Java. Mature programming languages like Java yielded substantially more findings than newer languages like Rust, likely because established languages have more developed SAST tool ecosystems rather than inherently worse code quality. These results suggest that developers should consider available SAST tooling when selecting implementation languages for security critical systems.

papers.title: Multi-quadratic equations associated with KdV-type equations
papers.abstract: The potential KdV equation admits dpKdV as a full discretization. Similarly, most KdV-type equations admit multi-quadratic quad equations as algebraic condition on Bäcklund transformation. These quad equations also yield three-point discrete symmetries and ensure the commutativity of two symmetries corresponding to different lattice directions. In each case, the quad equation is either an ABS equation or a multi-quadratic equation of the Atkinson--Nieszporski class. For KdV, mKdV, potential Gardner and exponential Calogero--Degasperis, these are the equations $H2^*$, $A1^*$, $Q1^*$ and $A2^*$, respectively, and for the elliptic Calogero--Degasperis equation it is the primary model $Q4^*$.

papers.title: Direction-Selective Anomalous Quantum Transport from Saddle-like Topological Surface States Coupled to an Electronic Instability in YbSb$_{2}$
papers.abstract: We report direction-selective anomalous quantum transport in epitaxial YbSb$_{2}$ thin films associated with an interplay between anisotropic topological surface states and an electronic instability. Quantum oscillations reveal a quasi-two-dimensional orbit with a non-trivial Berry phase and Dirac-like dispersion, observable for current along the $a$-axis but absent along the orthogonal in-plane $c$-axis. Together with first-principles calculations, these observations support its assignment to a saddle-like topological surface state. Its oscillation amplitude exhibits a field-dependent, non-monotonic temperature evolution that departs from conventional Lifshitz-Kosevich behavior. Raman and coherent phonon spectroscopy reveal additional low-temperature modes consistent with a density-wave instability. Their pronounced polarization anisotropy and colossal field-induced Raman enhancement suggest a strongly anisotropic, field-enhanced electronic susceptibility associated with the density-wave modes. Our findings point to dynamical coupling between anisotropic topological surface states and a field-responsive density-wave instability as a route to direction-selective anomalous quantum transport.

papers.title: Multiloop Unitarity from Airy Zeros
papers.abstract: Hidden zeros are non-trivial cancellations that make amplitudes or integrands vanish on specific kinematic loci away from propagator poles. They have been shown to uniquely determine tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands in $\Tr(ϕ^3)$ theory, without assuming factorization. Here we extend both the zeros and the uniqueness results to two, three and four loops at arbitrary multiplicity. We show that two types of zeros naturally enter the all-loop problem. First, tree-level zeros extend to all loop orders and fix relative weights within families of subgraphs attached to vacuum ``loop cores.'' We then show that Kontsevich's matrix Airy function can be used to generate a rich structure of loop level zeros that fix the relative weights of the loop cores themselves. The relative factorization and cut data required by unitarity therefore follow from the combination of tree and Airy loop zeros. These results bring within reach the emergence of unitarity to all orders in perturbation theory.

papers.title: High-Speed Control of a Fluxonium Qubit via Picosecond Pulses from Josephson Digital Circuits
papers.abstract: We develop a control strategy for fluxonium qubits based on picosecond single-flux-quantum (SFQ) pulses generated by Josephson digital circuits. A major challenge is that SFQ protocols originally designed for transmon control become inefficient for low-frequency fluxonium. In this regime, the asymmetry of flux and charge couplings leads either to excessive leakage or excessively long gate times. We show that this limitation can be overcome by two complementary protocols. The first protocol employs high-frequency SFQ pulse packets applied through the flux channel, offering a simple, analytically transparent, and robust approach for high-fidelity single-qubit control. The second protocol combines phase-shifted flux and charge pulse sequences to enhance the resonant drive and reduce the gate duration. Multilevel simulations demonstrate single-qubit gate fidelities above $99.99\%$; the simpler protocol remains robust under moderate variations of qubit parameters and flux bias, while the combined protocol preserves high fidelity while substantially accelerating the gate. These results establish SFQ-based cryogenic control as a realistic route to fast, accurate, and scalable manipulation of fluxonium qubits.

papers.title: The Unused Input: The Initial State as a Conditioning Interface for Recurrent TSFMs
papers.abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast unseen series without task-specific training. Increasingly they are built on recurrent backbones, whose constant per-step cost makes long-context inference cheap, and which, unlike transformers, carry a state. A recurrent backbone computes its prediction from two inputs: the observed context window and the initial recurrent state. In practice only the first is utilised and the initial state is unused by convention. We ask whether the initial state can be utilised in recurrent TSFMs. Using the xLSTM-based zero-shot forecaster TiRex as a case study, we freeze the backbone and train only a small head that writes a context vector into the initial state, so that any change in accuracy is attributable to the injected state rather than to adapted weights. A spectral summary of the input window, learned once and applied unchanged to every series, lowers mean GiftEval MASE by 0.175%, with every seed improving, which neither a parameter-matched LoRA adapter nor a learnable static state reproduces. An embedding of text attached to each series, evaluated on six MoTime datasets, reveals two roles for the state. As a per-dataset adaptation surface, a static state lowers MASE by 0.04-6.96% of the zero-shot baseline (8-70% of the gain of full fine-tuning). As a channel for exogenous information, the text-conditioned state lowers it by a further 0.15-0.41% of the zero-shot baseline on four of six datasets and, combined with a LoRA adapter, exceeds full fine-tuning, which has no access to the text, on one of them. In TiRex, the effect concentrates in the mLSTM blocks and is strongest at short context. The results are preliminary and the improvements small, but they point to the initial state as a direction for further research.

papers.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
papers.abstract: Rapidly evolving LLM architectures and heterogeneous mobile hardware make supporting new models in on-device inference engines a recurring and costly system challenge. Each model may require coordinated changes across conversion, graph construction, operators, and hardware backends. Existing coding agents often miss these cross-layer dependencies and struggle to diagnose failures across host--device execution paths. We present EngineAgent, an agentic system for automating on-device LLM model enablement. Its key insight is to separate reusable engine and hardware knowledge from model-specific implementation. Before enablement, EngineAgent constructs a hierarchy-aware engine index that captures engine abstraction layers and cross-layer dependencies, and pre-validates backend-specific build, execution, and debugging workflows using already supported models. For each new model, a builder uses this knowledge to coordinate cross-layer changes, while an auditor checks implementation completeness and drives iterative debugging through device-side validation. Across 12 tasks spanning three mobile LLMs and four engine--backend pairs on CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, EngineAgent achieves 75% end-to-end success with either of two underlying LLMs, versus 33.3% for the strongest coding-agent baseline. Success requires compilation, on-device execution, and output-logit agreement with reference implementations. EngineAgent also reduces average per-task time and model-API cost relative to baselines using the same underlying LLMs.

papers.title: CLADE: Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented systems often retrieve passages that are accurate and relevant but state the answer at a coarser level of granularity than the question requires. For example, a question may ask which specific disease a drug treats (familial hyperlipidemia), while the retrieved passage mentions the broader disease family (hyperlipidemia). Prior work on context sufficiency treats such coarse passages simply as insufficient. We argue that they form a distinct case, which we call resolvable insufficiency: text alone cannot settle the fine-grained answer, but the broader category it mentions maps to a short list of candidate answers in a domain ontology. When language models read these coarse, family-only passages, they exhibit a phenomenon we call Clade (Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence): they answer instead of abstaining or searching further. On biomedical questions from PrimeKG, family-only passages reduce abstention by 13.8 points compared to uninformative passages, and the resulting guesses are wrong about half the time. A counterfactual test confirms the cause: replacing an exact disease name with its broader family name lowers abstention by 17.4 points compared to deleting the sentence. Simple fixes like confidence filtering, scaling to a larger model, and explicitly instructing the model to abstain cannot resolve Clade, and this replicates on ecological species interactions in GloBI. Finally, we test whether an ontology can turn coarse passages into exact answers. Given the correct family, an ontology list includes the true answer in 98.5% of cases, but string matching finds that family on the page for only 19.8%. Letting the model choose the family raises this to 30.0% and end-to-end recovery from 10.0% to 26.8%. Overall, our results show when language models should stop guessing and consult an ontology, and highlight which steps of that process remain unsolved.

papers.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
papers.abstract: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. The dataset considered represents $10.6$ years of livetime and is three times larger than previous ARA neutrino searches. This search achieves a $28\%$ analysis efficiency for a neutrino flux corresponding to the current experimental upper limits. No neutrino candidates are observed on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. We set a new upper limit on the diffuse UHE neutrino flux, which is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV. We also discuss lessons learned for future searches on large radio arrays.

papers.title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
papers.abstract: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Padé resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

papers.title: The Symplectic Nature of Noncentral Reducible Stratum in SU(2) Character Variety
papers.abstract: Let \(Σ_g\) be a closed oriented surface of genus \(g\geq2\). The purpose of this paper is to use an explicit example, the representation of the surface group $π_1(Σ_g)$ into $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, to investigate the deformation space of the representation variety at a type of singular points, reducible but noncentral representations, and explore the geometric structure of the corresponding stratum in the representation variety and the character variety. In particular, the reduced tangent quadratic cone determines the symplectic structure at the reducible noncentral stratum of the character variety.
